Lesson No. 223: Explanation of Verses

Verses 1 to 3

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

This surah is the first of those seven surahs that begin with the disjointed letters (huruf muqatta'at) Ha Meem. In one of them, after Ha Meem, the letters Ain, Seen and Qaf also appear. Regarding the disjointed letters, we have said in all the surahs that they point to the fact that this speech is composed of these very letters of the alphabet, and that it is an inimitable speech, although these letters are within your reach. They are the letters of your language, and you both speak this language and write it.

After these letters, there is then an indication to the revelation of the Book. This is a matter that is often mentioned at the beginning of the Makki surahs, whose subject is mostly the Islamic worldview and the Kalima of Tawheed.

Tanzil ... al-Aleem (40:2): "The revelation of this Book is from Allah, who is Mighty and All-Knowing."

After this indication, the discourse now shifts to some attributes of the Being who has revealed this speech. These are the attributes that have a deep connection with the subject of this surah. The attributes of Allah are connected with the topics and issues that this surah takes up.

Ghafir al-Dhanb ... al-Maseer (40:3): "He is Mighty, All-Knowing, the Forgiver of sin and the Acceptor of repentance, severe in punishment and Bountiful. There is no god but He; to Him is the final return." In this verse, the attributes of might, knowledge, forgiveness of sins, acceptance of repentance, severe punishment, grace and generosity, the oneness of divinity and sovereignty, and the return of all people to Him are described. And all the themes of this surah revolve around the matters that have been set down in this verse. This verse is brought in a very forceful manner, with a powerful voice, and with strong phrases and sentences, with great firmness and steadfastness. Allah has introduced here those attributes of His that have a profound effect on human existence and human life. Thus Allah sharpened the feelings of people's hearts and their consciousness. He created hope within them and awakened expectation. He created fear and God-consciousness within them, and they were made to believe that they are in the control of Allah. They cannot flee anywhere from the disposal of Allah. Let us now examine these attributes in detail.

Al-Aziz (40:2): He who is powerful and absolutely capable, who prevails over everyone, and over whom no one can prevail. He disposes of all affairs, no one has power over Him, and there is no overseer above Him.

Al-Aleem (40:2): He is the One who runs this universe with knowledge and expertise; no secret of this universe is hidden from Him, and nothing is absent from His knowledge.

Ghafir al-Dhanb (40:3): He who forgives the sins of His servants, those servants whose sins, by His encompassing knowledge, Allah knows to be deserving of forgiveness.

Qabil al-Tawb (40:3): He who shows mercy to the disobedient, brings them back into His refuge of security, opens the door of His mercy for them, and lets them enter without hindrance or restriction.

Shadid al-Iqab (40:3): He who destroys the arrogant and punishes the enemies of Islam, who neither repent nor seek forgiveness.

Dhi al-Tawl (40:3): He who gives blessings to people, who increases good deeds and gives people so much that their blessings cannot be counted.

La ilaha illa Huwa (40:3): Divinity and sovereignty belong to Him alone, and He is One without partner, in His essence and attributes.

Ilayhi al-Maseer (40:3): For reckoning and accounting, everyone must present themselves before Him, and there is no place to flee from Him. And there will be a meeting with Him. All creation must return to Him, and He is the place of return.

Thus the relationship of the servants with Allah and of Allah with the servants is made clear. In the consciousness, concepts, perceptions and knowledge of the servants, their connection with Allah is established. In this way they come to know with what care and caution they must deal with Allah, and they must act knowing what displeases Allah and what pleases Him. As for those whose religions and beliefs are fabulous, they remain in bewilderment about the conception they hold of their deities. They have no firm information about those deities, and they do not know what angers them and with what they are pleased. The desires of those deities, as depicted by them, keep changing, and their inclination is not clear. Those deities are quickly affected. Such people live a life of constant restlessness with their deities and always search for where their pleasure lies and where it does not. Whether they are pleased with amulets, pleased with sacrifices, pleased with slaughtered animals, or otherwise. And even if they do these things, they still do not know whether they have become pleased or not.

In these circumstances Islam came. It gave clear and pure beliefs, and connected people with their true God. It made them aware of the correct attributes of Allah. It told them about the will of Allah, and it also made clear how they can draw near to Allah, how they can hope for His mercy, how they can fear His punishment, and what is the straight and correct path of Allah.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on surah 40, verses 4–6:

Verses 4 to 6

After the ruling that Allah possesses many attributes and that He is One without partner, it is now stated that these truths are accepted by everything in this universe, because the nature of the universe is bound up with these truths, and this connection is direct, with no dispute or argument. This whole universe accepts the signs of Allah with complete composure; it bears witness to Allah's Oneness. Those who argue about them are only those who have set themselves upon disbelief, and these people have turned away from this universe.

﴿Those who dispute about the signs of Allah, none do so except those who disbelieve﴾ (40:4). "Only those" means that from within this universe, only those who have set themselves upon disbelief deny these signs. From this great creation, only these people have deviated. And in relation to this magnificent existence, their standing is less than that of an ant, just as, in relation to this earth, an ant is an insignificant thing. In the same way, in relation to this universe, man is less than an ant. Yet this human being argues about the signs of Allah, while this great universe stands against the people of disbelief, acknowledges the Real Lord, and confesses the powers of the Mighty, the Compeller. These people, in this stance, stand against their own end. Even if they possess strength in the world, have status, wealth and authority, they have no concern for the place to which they must go.

﴿Let not their movement through the lands deceive you﴾ (40:4). "Let not their going about in the lands deceive you." However much they run about, however much power, wealth and status they hold, however much luxury they enjoy, in the end these people are destined for ruin and destruction. The outcome of their struggle is well known. Is it possible that a contest could take place between the Great Creator of the universe, this universe, and a tiny ant of this universe?

Before them, many nations like them passed over this earth. What became of them makes clear what the end of such nations is, those who set themselves against the power of Allah. Allah's power lays them low and crushes every power that rises to wage war against Allah.

﴿The people of Noah denied before them, and the factions after them; and every nation plotted against their messenger to seize him, and they argued with falsehood to refute the truth, so I seized them. Then how was My punishment?﴾ (40:5). "The people of Noah denied before them, and the factions after them as well. Every nation pounced upon its messenger to seize him. They all tried to humble the truth with the weapons of falsehood, but in the end I seized them. Then see how My punishment was." This line runs from the time of Noah (peace be upon him), and it is a battle that is fought in every time and place. This verse gives the summary of that story. The story of the messengers and their denial, and the arrogant attitude towards them and towards Allah, has been the same in every time and place, and the end has also been one.

A messenger comes, and the arrogant among his people deny him. They did not answer proof with proof; instead, they came with the weapons of violence against proof. They tried to seize the messenger and to throw dust into the eyes of the common people, in order to confront the truth and humble it. But the mighty power of Allah intervened, and seized such arrogant ones in such a way that they became a lesson for those who came after.

﴿Then how was My punishment?﴾ (40:5). In truth, Allah's punishment was destructive and very severe. Whatever traces of these nations remain today show that this punishment was very severe, and the narrations and traditions also tell that it was very severe. This battle did not end here; it continues until the Day of Resurrection.

﴿And thus the word of your Lord has come true against those who disbelieved, that they are the companions of the Fire﴾ (40:6). "Thus the decree of your Lord has become binding upon all those who committed disbelief, that they are destined for the Fire." When this decree of Allah is true, has been fixed, and has in effect been enforced, then every kind of debate ends.

In this way the Qur'an depicts a real situation: a portrayal of the long struggle between faith and disbelief, the battle between truth and falsehood, between those who call to Allah and those who act arrogantly on earth and speak without proof. Thus the Qur'an shows that this struggle between truth and falsehood has been underway since the beginning of humanity, and its field extends beyond the earth. It also continues throughout this whole universe, for the entire universe has submitted before Allah, while a disbeliever wages war not only against the believers but against the whole universe. He fights against the signs of Allah present within this universe, and the outcome of this struggle is also known: the forces of truth are very great and very powerful. There is Allah, there is the whole universe, there are the believers, and against them stands a small and insignificant force. Although for a time its side may have grown heavy and it may have appeared very frightening, in the end it is destined for destruction.

The reality that the struggle between truth and falsehood, the forces that fight in it, and its battlefield, which is the long span of human history, are portrayed by the Qur'an so that this truth may settle firmly in the hearts of the believers, especially those believers who carry the call to truth on the principles and method of the prophets and give the call to faith in every time and place. They must know well and be certain that the power of falsehood is nothing at all, even though it may appear puffed up for a limited time in a limited land. That power is not reality. The real truth is what the Book of Allah points to, which it calls the Word of Truth, and truth is what prevails. Allah is the most truthful, and His word is true.

Alongside this reality, that it is the call of truth and its bearers are the believers, those believers are included too who bear the Throne of Allah and those around it, who also stand in support of the believers. They constantly present the reports of the believers before Allah, seek forgiveness for them, and ask Allah to fulfil His promise to them. Why? Because these humans are also believers, and they too are believers.

Alongside this reality, that it is the call of truth and its bearers are the believers, those believers are included too who bear the Throne of Allah and those around it, who also stand in support of the believers. They constantly present the reports of the believers before Allah, seek forgiveness for them, and ask Allah to fulfil His promise to them. Why? Because these humans are also believers, and they too are believers.

We do not know the reality of the Throne ('Arsh), nor can we define its form, and we also do not know how those who bear it carry it. We do not know what its surroundings are like or what the angels around it are like. Therefore we should not waste effort trying to discover the form and essence of these things, since they lie beyond the scope of human perception. Nor should we pursue unseen matters about which those who engage in disputation have been given no knowledge. What is understood from the verses is only this: certain close servants of Allah glorify their Lord along with praising Him, they believe in Allah, and the Qur'an specifies their faith so that their connection with believing humans becomes clear, and these close servants of Allah pray for good for the believing humans who are engaged in the struggle between good and evil in this world. The manner in which these servants pray contains a lesson for us, that every human should address Allah in this way. They say:

﴿Our Lord, You encompass all things in mercy and knowledge﴾ (40:7). "O our Lord, You encompass everything with Your mercy and Your knowledge." They present their request for mercy before Allah in this way: they ask for that mercy for us humans which in reality encompasses everything, and they take as a means Allah's knowledge, which includes everything. They do not present to Allah anything new that is not within His knowledge. It is through Allah's mercy and knowledge, which encompass everything, that they make their supplication.

﴿So forgive those who have repented and followed Your way, and protect them from the punishment of the Hellfire﴾ (40:7). "So forgive, and save from the punishment of Hell, those who have repented and adopted Your path." In this prayer there is one allusion to forgiveness and repentance, which accords with the opening of the surah, "Forgiver of sin and Accepter of repentance," and the second allusion is to protection from the punishment of Hell, which accords with the opening of the surah, "Severe in punishment."

After this, these servants advance a little further in their prayer. Now they ask for more than forgiveness and protection from the punishment of Hell: they ask for the granting of Paradise, and they ask for the fulfilment of the promises that Allah has made to His righteous servants.

﴿Our Lord, and admit them into the Gardens of Eden which You have promised them, along with those among their fathers, spouses and offspring who are righteous. Indeed You are the Mighty, the Wise﴾ (40:8). "O our Lord, admit them into everlasting gardens which You have promised them, and along with them (also bring there) those of their parents, spouses and offspring who are righteous. Indeed You are the Almighty, the All-Wise." Admission into Paradise is certainly a great blessing and a very great success, and beyond that is the addition of fathers, spouses and children being with them. This is an additional blessing. It demonstrates that believers in Paradise will also be together in the form of a family system. It is faith that creates togetherness among fathers, spouses and children; were it not for faith, these ties would be severed. And the final result that follows from this phrase is:

﴿Indeed You are the Mighty, the Wise﴾ (40:8). "You are the Almighty and the All-Wise." In this there is power on one side and wisdom on the other. No decision concerning the servants can be made except by power and wisdom.

﴿And protect them from evil deeds; and whomsoever You protect from evil deeds on that Day, upon him You have indeed had mercy. That is the great success﴾ (40:9). "And protect them from misdeeds. Whomever You protect from misdeeds on the Day of Judgement, upon him You have truly shown mercy; and that is the great triumph." And this destruction becomes manifest in the Hereafter; they lead to the Fire. When Allah has protected the believers from misdeeds, they have been saved from Hell and from its evil consequences as well. This will be the pinnacle of divine mercy in that difficult time. And

﴿That is the great triumph﴾ (40:9). "That is the great success": that one is saved from misdeeds.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 40, verses 10–12:

Verses 10 to 12

Al-maqt (the meaning is extreme abhorrence). All of God's creation will call out to them from every side: "Woe to you! The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was calling you to faith, and you denied him without any right!" And Allah was greatly displeased with you, and He abhorred your conduct, just as today you have come to know the truth, and so you now abhor your conduct. But the time has already passed for you. You disbelieved, turned away from faith, and a great treasure has departed from you. This sign will come from the whole universe, and it will be a severe torment of the soul for them. On that dreadful day, instead of any consolation, there will be only more reproach from every side. Now the veils of deception and misguidance have been lifted from before their eyes, and they know that the place of salvation is now only the Divine Being. Therefore, they plead in supplication:

﴿They will say: "Our Lord, You have indeed given us life twice, and now we acknowledge our sins. Is there any way out from here?"﴾ (40:11). This is a request of a most wretched, despairing and ill-fated people. Now they say, "O our Lord," whereas at that time they used to deny the Lord. You gave us life the first time: You breathed a soul into the dead, and he came alive. Then You gave us life again after death, and now we are in the place of gathering. Therefore, You are capable of delivering us from the present calamity. Now we have acknowledged our sins.

﴿Is there any way of exit?﴾ (40:11). This is a rebuke, which reveals their restlessness, despair and bitterness. In this harsh time, they are also told the real cause of their evil end:

﴿That is because, when Allah alone was invoked, you disbelieved, but when others were associated with Him, you believed. So judgment belongs to Allah, the Most High, the Most Great.﴾ (40:12). This state in which you are afflicted is due to the fact that, when Allah alone was called to, you refused to accept it, and when others were joined with Him, you accepted it. Now the decision lies in the hand of Allah, the Exalted and Great, who has brought you, through this humiliating end, to the point where you denied the creed of Tawhid and accepted the creed of Shirk. Therefore, the decision now rests with Allah alone, who is Al-Ali and Al-Kabir. Both these attributes are appropriate for judgment: only one who is exalted and of great station can pass judgment, and Allah is above everything and greater than everything, especially on the Day of Judgment.

Here a glimpse of Allah's attributes, Al-Ali and Al-Kabir, is shown, and believers are commanded to make supplication at the court of this Al-Ali and Al-Kabir, to adopt the creed of Tawhid, and to take His system as their way of life. Here they are also warned of the moment of the Judgment of the Hereafter, when Allah, the One, the Subduer, will hold all authority, and He is supremely exalted.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 40, verses 13–17:

Verses 13 to 17

﴿Huwa alladhi yurikum ayatihi﴾ (40:13) "It is He who shows you His signs." The signs of Allah are found in every thing in this universe: in the movement of the sun and the moon, in the system of night and day, in thunder and lightning, in rain and showers, in the atom, in the cell, in the leaf and in the petals. In short, every thing is a miraculous sign, and the greatness of this sign becomes evident when a person sits down to copy it, or to create something like it. Yet, alas, if only he could copy any such thing or create something like it, or even create a very small thing like one of the creations of Allah.

﴿Wa yunazzilu lakum minas-sama'i rizqan﴾ (40:13) "And He sends down provision for you from the heavens." People know only about the rain, by which life on this earth is sustained, and which provides all the means of food and drink. The other things that descend from the heavens are also countless, and their revelations continue daily. Among them are the rays that give life; if they were not there, there would be no life on this star of the earth. This is also a mental and spiritual nourishment for man, which has been descending since Adam (peace be upon him), and through which man has advanced beyond infancy and reached maturity. And now, because of the Prophethood of Muhammad (ﷺ), he has begun to walk upon the straight path. And this Provider (al-Razzaq) has given him a way of life (manhaj hayat) and has bestowed upon him the permanent law of this universe.

﴿Wa ma yatadhakkaru illa man yunib﴾ (40:13) "And none takes heed except one who turns (to Allah) in repentance." The person who turns towards Allah knows how magnificent Allah's grace and bounty are, and he finds the signs of Allah in this universe, whereas the heedless and the hard-hearted do not pay attention to them. The remembrance of Allah that arises in the hearts of the believers because of their turning to Him, and their reflection upon these signs, is the basis on which the Muslims are called to call upon Allah alone, to establish the system of life that He has ordained, and to pay no heed to the displeasure of the disbelievers.

If the believers make their religion pure for Allah and establish only the Islamic system of life, then the disbelievers can never be pleased with them. Likewise, even if they call upon Allah alone, the disbelievers cannot be pleased. No matter how much gentleness the believers show towards the disbelievers, however much they compromise, and however much effort they make to win their approval, they will never be pleased with them. Therefore the believers should proceed fearlessly on their path: they should call upon the One Lord, adopt pure belief in Him, and turn hearts towards Allah, whether the disbelievers are pleased or displeased, for they will never be content.

Now it is explained what the attributes of that Allah are, whom the believers will turn towards in worship and against whom the disbelievers will express their displeasure. Those attributes are:

﴿Rafi'ud-darajati dhul-'arshi yulqi'r-ruha min amrihi 'ala man yasha'u min 'ibadih﴾ (40:15) "He is the Exalted in degrees, the Lord of the Throne; He sends down the Spirit by His command upon whomever of His servants He wills." Allah alone is the One of exalted ranks and high station. And He is the Lord of a Throne which holds sway over the entire universe and is most exalted; and it is He who sends down spiritual teachings upon His servant, and because of them this earth is revived, and the souls and hearts of the human beings living on it come to life. This refers to revelation and prophethood. But the manner of expression intends to show what the purpose and aim of revelation and prophethood are: that revelation is life and spirit for people. And it descends from the heights upon the chosen servants. All these attributes, images and colours are in harmony with the attribute by which Allah is described as al-'Aliyy al-Kabir (the Most High, the Great). Now, what is the duty entrusted to those who are chosen and upon whom the Spirit is sent down? Only to warn the people.

﴿Liyundhira yawma't-talaq﴾ (40:15) "So that he may warn of the Day of Mutual Meeting." On that day all people will meet one another, and people will confront their deeds. People will meet the angels, the jinn and all creatures, and all people will also have to meet the Lord and give account. Thus this day is the Day of Mutual Meeting in all its meanings. Furthermore, it will be a day when everything is laid open; no veil, no ornamentation, and no deception will prevail in it:

﴿Yawma hum barizun la yakhfa 'ala Allahi minhum shay'un﴾ (40:16) "The day when they will come forth, with nothing of theirs hidden from Allah." Nothing is ever hidden from Allah at any time, on any day, or in any state. But in other days, in the days of this world, people think they are hidden and that their deeds and movements are concealed. Today, even people themselves will realize that everything has been made manifest, that their good and bad lies open before them, that the veils have vanished, and that they stand before Allah.

Today the deniers and the arrogant will be humbled, shrunken and cowed; the whole universe will be terrified and people will be in dread. Sovereignty will belong to Allah alone, the One, the Subduer. Allah is always the sole King, but previously people did not see the sovereignty of Allah; today their hearts and minds acknowledge that sovereignty belongs to Allah. Every arrogant person will also know that the King is Allah alone. All kinds of clamour and uproar will cease that day, and a mighty and majestic voice will be heard, which will itself ask and itself answer, for in the whole universe today there is no one who could answer.

﴿Limani'l-mulk? Lillahi'l-wahidi'l-qahhar﴾ (40:16) "To whom belongs the Kingdom today? To Allah, the One, the Subduer."

﴿Al-yawma tujza kullu nafsin bima kasabat, la zulma al-yawm, inna Allaha sari'u'l-hisab﴾ (40:17) "Today every soul will be recompensed for what it earned; no injustice will be done today. Indeed, Allah is swift in reckoning." Today is the day of the recompense of truth. Today is the day of justice; today is the day of judgement and of pronouncing sentence. No respite is granted to anyone, and there is no slowness.

An awe and silence settle upon the atmosphere. Solemnity and fear overcome the people; all creation listens and is struck with dread. All matters are decided and all records are rolled up, with great haste. At the beginning of the surah it was said that those who dispute concerning the signs of Allah:

﴿La yaghurrannaka taqallubuhum fil-bilad﴾ (40:4) "Let not their movement about the lands deceive you." Here it has been shown that the consequence of their movement in the land, of their elevation and unjust pride, of their tyranny and dominance, and of their wealth and equipment, is that they are struck with fear and cannot even speak.

Now the address turns to the Holy Prophet (ﷺ), that he should warn his people of that severe day. A scene is presented in which the authority of judgement belongs to Allah alone, whereas earlier their circumstances on that day had been related in a narrative manner, and they had been given no permission to speak.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 40, verses 18–20:

Verses 18 to 20

Āzifah (الآزفة) means "the near one," the one that comes quickly; the meaning here is the Day of Judgment. This word draws a picture of the Hour as though it were about to arrive. Human breathing will become rapid, and people will be gasping, and hearts will be rising up to the throats, and a very great pressure will be upon people. Yet these anxious hearts will strive to face the pressure: they will hold back the rapidity of their breath, they will try to overcome grief, and they will conceal their fear. And because of this restraint, further pressure will be upon them, and their chests will be bursting. There will be no friend before whom they can open their hearts and who will sympathize, and no intercessor who will speak on their behalf. In such a terrifying and agonizing place, what can anyone say?

Their secrets will be revealed on that day, and nothing of theirs will be hidden from Allah. Even the treachery of the eyes will not remain hidden, and the secrets of the hearts will not remain hidden.

﴿Yaʿlamu khāʾinat al-aʿyuni wa mā tukhfi al-ṣudūr﴾ (40:19): "He knows the stealthy glance of the eyes, and what the breasts conceal." The treacherous eyes always keep their treachery hidden, but nothing is hidden from Allah, nor is the secret of hearts hidden; Allah knows everything. On that day, only Allah will judge. These will be true judgments. Those whom they had made into gods will have no authority, and they will be unable to judge.

﴿Wa-Allāhu yaqḍī bil-ḥaqq... shay'in﴾ (40:20): "And Allah judges with truth, while those whom they call upon besides Him do not judge anything." Allah makes judgments of truth with knowledge and perfect skill. He judges having seen and heard. He neither wrongs anyone nor forgets anything.

﴿Inna Allāha huwa al-Samīʿ al-Baṣīr﴾ (40:20): "Indeed, Allah is the All-Hearing, the All-Seeing."

﴿Yaʿlamu khāʾinat al-aʿyuni wa mā tukhfi al-ṣudūr﴾ (40:19): "He knows the stealthy glance of the eyes, and what the breasts conceal." The treacherous eyes always keep their treachery hidden, but nothing is hidden from Allah, nor is the secret of hearts hidden; Allah knows everything. On that day, only Allah will judge. These will be true judgments. Those whom they had made into gods will have no authority, and they will be unable to judge.

﴿Wa-Allāhu yaqḍī bil-ḥaqq... shay'in﴾ (40:20): "And Allah judges with truth, while those whom they call upon besides Him do not judge anything." Allah makes judgments of truth with knowledge and perfect skill. He judges having seen and heard. He neither wrongs anyone nor forgets anything.

﴿Inna Allāha huwa al-Samīʿ al-Baṣīr﴾ (40:20): "Indeed, Allah is the All-Hearing, the All-Seeing."

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 40, verses 18–20:

Verses 18 to 20

Āzifah (الآزفة) means "the near one," the one that comes quickly; the meaning here is the Day of Judgment. This word draws a picture of the Hour as though it were about to arrive. Human breathing will become rapid, and people will be gasping, and hearts will be rising up to the throats, and a very great pressure will be upon people. Yet these anxious hearts will strive to face the pressure: they will hold back the rapidity of their breath, they will try to overcome grief, and they will conceal their fear. And because of this restraint, further pressure will be upon them, and their chests will be bursting. There will be no friend before whom they can open their hearts and who will sympathize, and no intercessor who will speak on their behalf. In such a terrifying and agonizing place, what can anyone say?

Their secrets will be revealed on that day, and nothing of theirs will be hidden from Allah. Even the treachery of the eyes will not remain hidden, and the secrets of the hearts will not remain hidden.

Lesson No. 224: At a Glance

Earlier we gave a general overview of this lesson. Before the detailed explanation, it should be noted that the story is brought here in keeping with the theme of the surah, and it is aligned with the manner of expression of this surah; in fact, some of the very phrases of this surah have been used, and the same style has been adopted. For example, the speech that the believing man (Rajul Mu'min) makes before Pharaoh contains some phrases that already appear earlier in this same surah. He advises Pharaoh, Haman and Qarun that you move about freely on the earth, and he warns them of a day like the one that befell the other peoples. And he warns them of the Day of Resurrection in the same way that the scenes of the Resurrection were mentioned earlier in the surah. He repeats what the end of those will be who dispute concerning the signs of Allah. The mention of Allah's displeasure, and the anger of the believers, as was mentioned in the previous lesson. After this, the scene of their state in Hell, where they will request to be taken out but their request will not be granted, just as a similar scene was mentioned before.

The entire speech of the believing man repeats the themes of this surah, and from this it becomes known that the believers all think in one way. It also shows that through this speech the atmosphere of the surah becomes uniform. A personality of this surah comes into view whose features are clear, and this is the characteristic that has been kept in view throughout the Qur'an.

Lesson No. 224: Explanation of the Verses

Verses 21 to 22

These verses serve as a bridge between the story of Musa and the earlier themes of the surah. They remind the polytheists of Makkah: reflect a little upon these historical events, and take a lesson from those that occurred right around you. Travel through the earth and reflect upon the events of the destruction of the earlier peoples, who adopted the same attitude toward the truth that you have adopted. They were stronger than you in power and in leaving marks upon the earth, but despite their mighty civilization and culture they were powerless before the punishment of Allah. Because of their sins they had gone far from the true center of strength. Thus their sins invited the believers to rise for their destruction, those with whom the powers of Allah, the Mighty, the Subduer, were helpers and supporters.

﴿So Allah seized them for their sins, and they had no protector from Allah﴾ (40:21). Because the thing that protects is faith and righteous deeds, and they were deprived of this. Then, the thing that protects is that a person be with faith, righteous deeds and the front of truth; but they were deniers and rejecters of Allah's signs, and what else could the end of such things be but ruin and destruction?

﴿That was because their messengers came to them with clear proofs, and they refused to believe. So Allah seized them. Indeed He is Strong and severe in punishment﴾ (40:22). After this general and principled indication, Allah now presents one example from among such peoples. These people were far stronger than the polytheists of Makkah and had left many marks upon the earth. Because of their sins Allah seized them. They were Pharaoh, Qarun and Haman, and along with them were the groups of those who posed as great ones.

The story of Musa (peace be upon him) consists of several parts and scenes. It begins at the point where Musa conveys Allah's message before Pharaoh, and its outcome is that, in the Hereafter, having been thrown into Hell, they dispute with one another in the Fire. This is a very long journey, but here the account is confined to glimpses of that long journey, and these glimpses show all the parts of the story that are required here.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 40, verses 23–24:

Verses 23–24

This is the encounter with Pharaoh. Moses stands with his miracles, and with him is that awe which accompanies every truth, and the truth is in his hand. Pharaoh, Haman and Qarun are also present. With them are their crooked and false position, their apparent power, and the rank and status whose loss they greatly fear. These people cannot confront the truth. So they now resort to futile debate and argument. Thus they say: ﴿A lying sorcerer﴾ (40:24).

Here the parts of the story that came after this debate are now cut out. The part of the contest with the sorcerers is also omitted, when they saw that Moses' staff had swallowed all their false magic and tricks, and they believed. Thus, having cut all these parts, the measures that the Pharaohites took after their defeat on the field are brought forward.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 40, verses 23–24:

Verses 23–24

This is the encounter with Pharaoh. Moses stands with his miracles, and with him is that awe which accompanies every truth, and the truth is in his hand. Pharaoh, Haman and Qarun are also present. With them are their crooked and false position, their apparent power, and the rank and status whose loss they greatly fear. These people cannot confront the truth. So they now resort to futile debate and argument. Thus they say: ﴿A lying sorcerer﴾ (40:24).

Here the parts of the story that came after this debate are now cut out. The part of the contest with the sorcerers is also omitted, when they saw that Moses' staff had swallowed all their false magic and tricks, and they believed. Thus, having cut all these parts, the measures that the Pharaohites took after their defeat on the field are brought forward.

Verse 25

This has always been the way of all the arrogant. When they run out of the weapons of argument and proof, they take up the weapons of oppression. Whenever they are humiliated by arguments and fear that the truth will prevail, because its words are clear and forceful, plain and comprehensible, touching the heart and appealing to human nature, just as the nature of the sorcerers accepted it, and they believed, although they had been brought for the contest. Having accepted the truth, they began to confront Pharaoh, although he was a very great tyrant. The comment on this is most fitting: "The plot of the disbelievers came to nothing."

Now, what do Pharaoh, Haman and Qarun do? They said:

﴿Kill the sons of those who believe with him, and spare their women﴾ (40:25). Pharaoh had issued this kind of command at the time of the birth of Musa (peace be upon him). It is possible that, after the decree had been issued earlier, the Pharaoh who issued this order died, and his son and heir became Pharaoh, and in the new era this oppressive decree became a dead law. When Musa came and invited Pharaoh, he knew him, because Musa had been raised in the royal palace. This new Pharaoh also knew that the previous government had issued a decree against the Children of Israel that their women should be spared and their men killed. So his courtiers may have advised that the same decree be enforced again against those who believed in Musa, whether they were Egyptian sorcerers, Children of Israel, or other people who had accepted Musa's call. It is also possible that the Pharaoh was the same one who had raised Musa (peace be upon him), but that his earlier decree had been softened, and its enforcement was no longer severe, and now his advisors again advised that this law be applied only to those who believed in Musa, in order to frighten them. As for Pharaoh himself, it appears that his opinion was different. He used to say that Musa would change your religion and the peace and security of the country would be destroyed, so allow me to rid you of Musa.

Verse 26

Pharaoh's words, "Leave me, that I may kill Musa" (40:26), show that the people around him were offering arguments against killing Musa (peace be upon him): that even if you kill Musa, the matter will not end, because the common masses will regard them as martyrs and make him a sacred figure. In this way, people will consciously rise up in support of his religion, especially since on a national festival day the sorcerers have already believed in him and have also told the people the reason for their faith. Yet the sorcerers had been gathered so that they might prove his religion false. It is also possible that some of the king's advisers were secretly afraid that the God of Musa would take revenge on them and they would be seized by God's punishment. This is not unlikely, because idol-worshippers believed in many gods, and they could naturally think that the God of Musa might take revenge on them. And Pharaoh's words, "And let him call upon his Lord" (40:26), though apparently an arrogant statement of Pharaoh, may perhaps be a reply to those advisers. And because of this arrogant statement, Allah later seized him and destroyed him, as will come later. This is a very interesting point, what Pharaoh said regarding the permissibility of killing Musa.

"Indeed I fear that he will change your religion, or that he will cause corruption in the land" (40:26). The argument of Pharaoh needs consideration. Is it a new thing for an idol-worshipping king to say, "I fear that he will change your religion, or at least will certainly cause corruption in the country"?

This is not a new matter. Every rebellious and corrupt person always says this whenever the reformist call of Islam begins. The corrupters said the same thing: they called reform corruption. Always, against the believing callers and reformers, self-interested rebels and corrupters presented this same excuse before the common people.

Whenever a struggle between truth and falsehood began, the logic and reasoning of falsehood remained this same. In the battle between faith and disbelief this same logic continued. In every time and place, and in every era of history, reform has been called corruption and corruption has been called reform. In short, this is an ancient story, and it is repeated again and again. But Musa (peace be upon him) was a servant of Allah. His trust was in an extremely strong power. He was protected in an impregnable fortress, and he had taken refuge in that Being with whom every rebellious arrogant person's people flee for refuge.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 40, verse 27:

Verse 27

Musa (Moses) said this and became composed, and entrusted the matter of his protection to that Being who is exalted above every arrogant person, who is above every tyrant, and who protects those who flee to His refuge from all other tyrants. He said that they were under the protection of the Lord who is their Lord and our Lord too. Allah has not forgotten us, nor has He left us unsupported against the threats of Fir'awn (Pharaoh). These people do not believe in the Day of Reckoning, and therefore they establish their greatness upon the earth. Anyone who believes in accountability on the Day of Judgment cannot become arrogant, for he can picture how humiliated, terrified and frightened people will be on the Day of Judgment. There will be no power, no might and no support; there will be no friend and no intercessor, and no ransom can be paid.

Now a man from among Fir'awn's own courtiers comes onto the scene. Truth has affected his heart, but he has kept his faith hidden for now. This man raises his voice in defence of Musa, and tries to make the people refrain from killing Musa. In his speech he addresses various aspects of the matter. He tries to instill his counsel into their hearts, stirs up their good feelings, tries to reassure them, and also warns them of an evil end.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran (Urdu translation)) on surah 40, verse 28–35 (part 1 of 2):

Verses 28 to 35

This is the magnificent discourse which the believing man (rajul mu'min) held with the scheming courtiers. He spoke in a most natural manner, with great caution, with great skill and forceful expression. First, he said that the proposal you are putting forward is a most abhorrent proposal.

﴿Do you kill a man merely because he says, "My Lord is Allah"?﴾ (40:28)

Is it a crime for someone to hold the belief that there is one God? It is everyone's right to hold the belief in which his heart and soul find contentment. Does anyone deserve to have his life taken on account of a belief? This is a most detestable and oppressive matter, and its repugnance, its wickedness and its vileness are entirely evident.

Then this man takes a step further: this man who says, "My Lord is only Allah," does not speak without proof; he speaks by presenting arguments, evidence and miracles.

﴿And indeed he has come to you with clear proofs from your Lord﴾ (40:28). This refers to the miracles which Moses (peace be upon him) presented. They witnessed them with their own eyes, and in their lofty gatherings, far from the common people, they can neither deny these miracles nor doubt them.

Now this man, by way of supposition, presents to them the evil consequences of this action and offers a fair resolution of the matter: at most, this is what you can suppose about him.

﴿If he is a liar, then his lie will be upon himself﴾ (40:28). He himself will be responsible for his lie; he will reach his end and receive the punishment for his crime. How can you kill a person merely for telling a lie?

But there is also another possibility, that this man may be truthful. Therefore, as a precaution, keep this in view as well, and do not make yourselves deserving of evil consequences.

﴿But if he is truthful, some of that which he threatens you with will befall you﴾ (40:28). Keep in view that some of the things with which he frightens you may indeed come upon you. This man does not warn you of all matters; rather, to reduce the debate, he mentions the possibility of only some of them, that is, he makes his speech fair. Now he speaks of a further principle which may apply to both parties, although the implicit allusion is directed at them.

﴿Indeed, Allah does not guide one who is a transgressor and a liar﴾ (40:28). If Moses is a liar, Allah will not grant him guidance or success. Then leave him to reach his end. And if you are the liars, and Moses speaks the truth while you are exceeding bounds concerning him, then the punishment of Allah may come upon you.

When he had frightened them with the statement that Allah does not guide those who exceed bounds and are liars, he now further says: if the punishment of Allah comes upon us, who can save us from the punishment of Allah? This is because we are not giving thanks for the present power, sovereignty and authority; we are being ungrateful for favours, and we are going to kill a man by the strength of our might.

﴿O my people, yours is the kingdom today, you being dominant in the land; but who will help us against the might of Allah should it come upon us?﴾ (40:29). This man possesses the complete awareness which a true believer possesses: that the punishment of Allah first descends upon kings, those in power and those with authority on earth, and they should fear the punishment of Allah more. This punishment is awaiting you every moment of night and day. Therefore this man reminds them that you are the supreme authorities of the earth, kings; so you should fear Allah far more than they do. This sentiment is part of the feelings of this believing man, and when he speaks of the punishment of Allah, he includes himself among them.

﴿Who then will help us against the might of Allah should it come upon us?﴾ (40:29).

When the discourse reached this point, there arose in Pharaoh the same reaction which arises in every rebel. False pride drives a person to evil, and such a person regards even pure advice as an attack on his kingdom and authority, and he assumes that the one giving advice seeks a share in power.

﴿Pharaoh said, "I only show you what I see, and I guide you only to the path of right conduct."﴾ (40:29). I tell you only what I consider correct, and I am convinced that it is beneficial and is the right path. Obviously, what a rebellious dictator thinks is the correct thing. How can anyone be permitted to think that kings may also think wrongly, or who has the right to hold a different opinion in the presence of a king or dictator? If this were possible, then of what are they kings and dictators!

But the faith of the believing man requires him to hold a consistent view against the king. Then the requirement of faith is that he warn them, admonish them and advise them, and openly express his sincere opinion. He should regard it as his duty to support the opinion he considers to be the truth, whatever the opinion of rebels, dictators and kings may be. Therefore this believing man knocks upon their hearts and minds from another angle, in the hope that they may perceive, awaken, be stirred within, and become gentle; so he draws their attention to the evil end of rebellious nations in history. History contains countless events which show that Allah has seized those who rebel and exceed bounds.

﴿And the one who believed said, "O my people, I fear for you a day like the day of the factions, like the custom of the people of Noah and 'Ad and Thamud and those after them. And Allah does not intend any injustice to the servants."﴾ (40:30–31). Each faction had a day of its own. But the believing man summed up all the separate days as one single day.

﴿Like the day of the factions﴾ (40:30): it was, as it were, one single day, of one kind, although the factions were many.

﴿And Allah does not intend any injustice to the servants﴾ (40:31). Allah seizes them for their sins. And by observing the end of these people, others who dwell around them are reformed, and those who come after these destroyed nations take admonition. Now this believing man knocks upon their hearts once more, and reminds them of the great day among the days of Allah, the Day of Judgement. It is called here the day of wailing.

﴿And O my people, I fear for you the day of calling out, the day when you will turn your backs and flee, with none to protect you from Allah. And whomever Allah leaves astray, there is no guide for him.﴾ (40:32–33)

Tanawwul means mutual calling out. On that day the angels will bring people to reckoning, and will call out to one another giving commands. Then the companions of the Heights will call out to the people of Paradise, and will also call out to the people of Hell, and the people of Hell will call out to the people of Paradise. Thus in various forms people will call out to one another. Therefore the Day of Resurrection is called the Day of Calling (yawm al-tanad), which includes mutual shouting and wailing. There will be running and commotion from every direction. This meaning accords with the statement of the believing man.

﴿The day you turn your backs and flee, with none to protect you from Allah﴾ (40:33). They will try to flee from the fear of Hell, but they will not be able to escape. The depiction here of wailing, flight and being seized is most fitting for the arrogant who hold rank here, so that they may know what your condition will be there.

﴿And whomever Allah leaves astray, there is no guide for him﴾ (40:33). In this there is an implicit allusion to Pharaoh's statement:

﴿And I guide you only to the path of right conduct﴾ (40:29). The allusion is that the path of guidance is the one Allah shows, and the path shown by Pharaoh is not the one Allah has shown, because Allah knows well the reality of people and their circumstances, what the path of guidance for them is and what misguidance is.

At the end, this believing man reminds them of what they had done regarding Joseph (peace be upon him). Moses (peace be upon him) was from among their offspring. The Egyptians had doubted the prophethood of Joseph, even though he came with signs and clear evidences. Therefore do not repeat with Moses the same treatment. He is confirming the truth of Moses too. You doubted the teachings of Joseph and established the false notion that after Joseph, Allah would never send any messenger. Moses came a long time after Joseph, and has refuted your belief that prophethood has ended.

﴿Joseph had already come to you with clear proofs, but you remained in doubt about what he brought. Then when he died, you said, "Allah will never send a messenger after him." Thus Allah leaves astray whoever is a transgressor and a doubter﴾ (40:34). Those who dispute concerning the signs of Allah without any authority or proof having come to them: it is greatly detested in the sight of Allah and of those who believe. Thus Allah sets a seal upon the heart of every arrogant tyrant.﴾ (40:34–35)

This is the only place in the Qur'an which alludes to the prophethood of Joseph, that he was sent as a messenger to the people of Egypt. From Surah Yusuf we learn that the treasures of Egypt were handed over to him. He was disposing of them with full authority, and he had attained the rank of "the Aziz of Egypt." It appears that this was the title of the Egyptian chief minister at that time. Surah Yusuf also mentions that he sat upon the throne of Egypt, although it is not certain that he became king of Egypt.

﴿And he raised his parents upon the throne, and they fell down before him in prostration. And he said, "O my father, this is the interpretation of my dream from before; my Lord has made it true."﴾ (Yusuf 12:100)

It is possible that the throne on which he seated his parents was some other distinguished place, and not the throne of the kingdom of Egypt on which Pharaohs used to sit. But these verses certainly prove that Joseph had attained supreme authority. Thus we can understand the meaning of the believing man's statement, that they had doubts about the teachings of Joseph. However, since Joseph was at a very high position of authority, people did not raise their voices in opposition to him.

﴿Until, when he died, they said, "Allah will never send a messenger after him."﴾ (40:34). It appears that his death brought them great joy, and they expressed this joy in the form of ending prophethood, because perhaps they did not like his teachings, for he taught pure monotheism. This teaching is clear from his speech in the prison.

﴿Are many lords better, or Allah, the One, the Irresistible?﴾ (12:39). They adopted this belief so that no messenger would come after Joseph; therefore they wished it to be so. Sometimes a person greatly likes a thing, and then he affirms that this matter has occurred, because in this way his desire is fulfilled.

The manner of the believing man becomes somewhat severe here, when he says that you doubt and, exceeding all bounds, you deny.

﴿Thus does Allah leave astray whoever is a transgressor and a doubter﴾ (40:34). This believing man warns them that whoever transgresses concerning the call which Allah has sent with signs, and doubts it, Allah will lead him astray; he is watching this. After this he tells them with great severity that those who dispute concerning the signs of Allah without any argument or proof are detested by the believers and by Allah, because their conduct is very evil. This man also criticizes their arrogance and their oppressive conduct, and warns them of the seizing of Allah, and it is the practice of Allah that He ultimately seizes tyrants and oppressors!

﴿Those who dispute concerning the signs of Allah without any authority that has come to them. It is greatly detested in the sight of Allah and of those who believe. Thus Allah sets a seal upon the heart of every arrogant tyrant.﴾ (40:35). The matter which was stated through the words of the believing man was also stated directly at the beginning of the surah: that those who dispute concerning the signs of Allah without proof, there is no place for guidance in their hearts, and their minds cannot reach the perception of truth.

Despite the lengthy speech of the believing man, in which he showed them the ups and downs of history and sought to move them, Pharaoh continued forward in his misguidance and made no effort to recognize the truth. Yet, apparently, he adopted the foolish attitude of investigating the claim of Musa (peace be upon him). In any case, the speech of the believing man had this effect: that

Pharaoh was inclined, in some manner, to undertake an inquiry into this movement. Thus Pharaoh did not directly reject the opinion of the council of elders.

Is it a crime for someone to hold the belief that there is one God? It is everyone's right to hold the belief in which his heart and soul find contentment. Then this man takes a step further: this man who says, "My Lord is only Allah," does not speak without proof; he speaks by presenting arguments, evidence and miracles.

﴿And indeed he has come to you with clear proofs from your Lord﴾ (40:28). This refers to the miracles which Moses (peace be upon him) presented. They witnessed them with their own eyes, and in their lofty gatherings, far from the common people, they can neither deny these miracles nor doubt them.

﴿If he is a liar, then his lie will be upon himself﴾ (40:28). He himself will be responsible for his lie; he will reach his end and receive the punishment for his crime. How can you kill a person merely for telling a lie?

﴿But if he is truthful, some of that which he threatens you with will befall you﴾ (40:28). Keep in view that some of the things with which he frightens you may indeed come upon you. This man does not warn you of all matters; rather, to reduce the debate, he mentions the possibility of only some of them, that is, he makes his speech fair. ﴿Indeed, Allah does not guide one who is a transgressor and a liar﴾ (40:28). If Moses is a liar, Allah will not grant him guidance or success. Then leave him to reach his end. When he had frightened them with the statement that Allah does not guide those who exceed bounds and are liars, he now further says: if the punishment of Allah comes upon us, who can save us from the punishment of Allah? This is because we are not giving thanks for the present power, sovereignty and authority; we are being ungrateful for favours, and we are going to kill a man by the strength of our might.

﴿O my people, yours is the kingdom today, you being dominant in the land; but who will help us against the might of Allah should it come upon us?﴾ (40:29). This man possesses the complete awareness which a true believer possesses: that the punishment of Allah first descends upon kings, those in power and those with authority on earth, and they should fear the punishment of Allah more. Therefore this man reminds them that you are the supreme authorities of the earth, kings; so you should fear Allah far more than they do. ﴿Who then will help us against the might of Allah should it come upon us?﴾ (40:29).

When the discourse reached this point, there arose in Pharaoh the same reaction which arises in every rebel. False pride drives a person to evil, and such a person regards even pure advice as an attack on his kingdom and authority, and he assumes that the one giving advice seeks a share in power.

﴿Pharaoh said, "I only show you what I see, and I guide you only to the path of right conduct."﴾ (40:29). I tell you only what I consider correct, and I am convinced that it is beneficial and is the right path. Obviously, what a rebellious dictator thinks is the correct thing. How can anyone be permitted to think that kings may also think wrongly, or who has the right to hold a different opinion in the presence of a king or dictator? If this were possible, then of what are they kings and dictators!

But the faith of the believing man requires him to hold a consistent view against the king. Then the requirement of faith is that he warn them, admonish them and advise them, and openly express his sincere opinion. He should regard it as his duty to support the opinion he considers to be the truth, whatever the opinion of rebels, dictators and kings may be. Therefore this believing man knocks upon their hearts and minds from another angle, in the hope that they may perceive, awaken, be stirred within, and become gentle; so he draws their attention to the evil end of rebellious nations in history. History contains countless events which show that Allah has seized those who rebel and exceed bounds.

He should regard it as his duty to support the opinion he considers to be the truth, whatever the opinion of rebels, dictators and kings may be. Therefore this believing man knocks upon their hearts and minds from another angle, in the hope that they may perceive, awaken, be stirred within, and become gentle; so he draws their attention to the evil end of rebellious nations in history. History contains countless events which show that Allah has seized those who rebel and exceed bounds.

﴿And the one who believed said, "O my people, I fear for you a day like the day of the factions, like the custom of the people of Noah and 'Ad and Thamud and those after them. ﴿Like the day of the factions﴾ (40:30): it was, as it were, one single day, of one kind, although the factions were many.

﴿And Allah does not intend any injustice to the servants﴾ (40:31). Allah seizes them for their sins. Now this believing man knocks upon their hearts once more, and reminds them of the great day among the days of Allah, the Day of Judgement. It is called here the day of wailing.

Then the companions of the Heights will call out to the people of Paradise, and will also call out to the people of Hell, and the people of Hell will call out to the people of Paradise. Thus in various forms people will call out to one another. Therefore the Day of Resurrection is called the Day of Calling (yawm al-tanad), which includes mutual shouting and wailing. There will be running and commotion from every direction. This meaning accords with the statement of the believing man.

﴿The day you turn your backs and flee, with none to protect you from Allah﴾ (40:33). They will try to flee from the fear of Hell, but they will not be able to escape. The depiction here of wailing, flight and being seized is most fitting for the arrogant who hold rank here, so that they may know what your condition will be there.

﴿And I guide you only to the path of right conduct﴾ (40:29). The allusion is that the path of guidance is the one Allah shows, and the path shown by Pharaoh is not the one Allah has shown, because Allah knows well the reality of people and their circumstances, what the path of guidance for them is and what misguidance is.

Despite the lengthy speech of the believing man, in which he showed them the ups and downs of history and sought to move them, Pharaoh continued forward in his misguidance and made no effort to recognize the truth. Yet, apparently, he adopted the foolish attitude of investigating the claim of Musa (peace be upon him). In any case, the speech of the believing man had this effect: that

Pharaoh was inclined, in some manner, to undertake an inquiry into this movement. Thus Pharaoh did not directly reject the opinion of the council of elders.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 40, verses 36–37:

Verses 36 to 37

Pharaoh said to Haman: "Build for me a lofty tower, that I may reach the routes of the heavens and look upon the god of Moses. Indeed, I think him to be a liar."

﴿And I think him to be a liar﴾ (40:37). This is the cunning and guesswork of the arrogant Pharaoh. He does not wish to come out openly against the truth, nor does he acknowledge the creed of Tawhid (the Oneness of God), because in that case his rule would end. The myths upon which his kingdom stood would be declared false after the creed of Tawhid. It is hard to believe that Pharaoh was so lacking in understanding, or that he was a man of such intellectual standing, that he would try to deceive the god of Moses in this simplistic manner, since the Pharaohs of Egypt were highly advanced in knowledge. In truth, this was a mockery on his part of Prophet Moses and the Lord of the worlds. Yet, with this mockery, he wished to make his conduct appear outwardly just. And this crude method and stratagem was his way of escaping the powerful logical speech that the believing man had delivered. Nevertheless, all these matters make it clear that the Pharaoh of Egypt insisted upon his misguidance, was afflicted with pride, and was determined to harass Moses.

﴿Thus was the evil of Pharaoh's deeds made attractive to him, and he was barred from the way﴾ (40:37). And now he became deserving of being barred from the path, because the attitude he displayed was a far-off deviation from the Straight Path. The conclusion drawn is that he was heading towards ruin and failure.

﴿And the scheming of Pharaoh led only to ruin﴾ (40:37). The whole of his cunning went only into the path of destruction.

Seeing this mockery, deception and persistence in misguidance, the believing man also deemed it appropriate to say one final word to them. It is a very lofty and clear statement. Earlier, he had invited the people: "Follow me, I guide you to the right path." Then he informed the people that this life is very brief and transient, so you should arrange for the life that endures, and protect yourselves from the everlasting punishment of the Hereafter. And he clearly explained what weaknesses lie in the belief in polytheism:

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 40, verses 38–44:

Verses 38–44

These are the realities that were stated plainly at the beginning of this surah. Here the believing man (rajul mu'min) repeats them in his address before Pharaoh. He says before Pharaoh:

﴿Yā qawmi ittabi'ūnī ahdikum sabīl al-rashād﴾ (40:38) "O my people, follow me; I will show you the right path." Just a few moments earlier, Pharaoh had said: ﴿Wa mā ahdīkum illā sabīl al-rashād﴾ (40:29) "And I show you nothing but the path of right guidance." The believing man's words are, in effect, a clear challenge to Pharaoh despite his kingdom and his tyranny and domination. This challenge is being issued while Haman and Qarun are also sitting in his presence. As the narrations report, both of them were Pharaoh's ministers. The believing man, before them, unfolds the reality of worldly life thus:

﴿Innamā hādhihi al-ḥayāh al-dunyā matā'un﴾ (40:39) "This worldly life is only a passing enjoyment." It is a provision that is bound to vanish, and it has no permanence or lasting stability.

﴿Wa inna al-ākhirata hiya dār al-qarār﴾ (40:39) "And the Hereafter is indeed the abode of permanence." The Hereafter is the real thing, and it should be kept more in view. Then he states this matter plainly:

﴿Man 'amila sayyi'atan fa-lā yujzā illā mithlahā...ḥisāb﴾ (40:40) "Whoever does an evil deed will be recompensed only with its equivalent, and whoever does righteous deeds, whether male or female, provided they are believers, all such people will enter Paradise, where they will be given provision without reckoning."

The mercy and grace of Allah require that good deeds be multiplied and rewarded without reckoning, and that evil deeds not be multiplied. This is Allah's kindness: He has taken account of the weaknesses of His servants. To make good and righteous deeds attractive, Allah has kept their reward great, so that people may remain firm and steadfast on this path. Allah has made good deeds an expiation for evil deeds and sins, and when they reach Paradise after this gentle reckoning, they will be given there without any reckoning or account.

The believing man also criticises them in his address. He calls them to the path of salvation, to the Gardens, while they call him to the Fire. He says in a tone of reproach:

﴿Wa yā qawmi...ilā al-nār﴾ (40:41) "O my people, what is this matter? I call you to salvation, and you call me to the Fire." Outwardly they did not call him to the Fire; they called him to shirk. It is clear that there is no difference between calling to shirk and calling to the Fire. It is one and the same thing, and the next verse makes the matter clear.

﴿Tad'ūnanī li-akfura...al-ghaffār﴾ (40:42) "You invite me to disbelieve in Allah and to associate with Him those things of which I have no knowledge, while I invite you to the Mighty, the Great Forgiver."

There is a very great difference between these two calls. My call is very clear and plain. This call from the Mighty, the Forgiving, is a call to the one God, Allah, whose oneness is witnessed by all the signs of this universe, and upon whose power and wisdom every thing in this universe is a witness that bears testimony. He calls them to the One who forgives, so that He may pardon them, the One who is the Greatest Forgiver. And to what do these people call this believing man? To disbelief and to shirk, of which they have no knowledge. It is mere assertion, illusions, and fables in which their belief rests. He tells them plainly that those beings whom you have made partners with Allah have no position in this world and no position in the Hereafter. Ultimately, all human beings must return only to Allah. And as for you who commit excess and transgress the limits, there is nothing for you but Hell.

﴿Lā jarama...aṣḥāb al-nār﴾ (40:43) "Truly, what you call me to has no call in this world or in the Hereafter, and our return is to Allah, and the transgressors are the people of the Fire."

After stating these fundamental matters of belief clearly, nothing else remains. The believing man made all these points before Pharaoh, his courtiers and ministers, without any hesitation or wavering. Earlier he had kept his faith hidden, but at the end of his address he declared it openly. Now only this remains: that, having discharged the duty of conveying the truth, he leave all matters to Allah. He has said his word, his conscience is at peace, and he has also said: "You will soon remember what I say to you, but at that time this advice will be of no benefit to you." In reality, the reins of affairs are in the hand of Allah.

﴿Fa-satadhkurūna mā aqūlu lakum...bil-'ibād﴾ (40:44) "Soon you will remember what I am saying to you. I entrust my affair to Allah; He is the Seer of His servants."

Here this address and dialogue comes to an end. The believing man recorded the word of truth in the conscience of this universe, and the Qur'an granted it everlasting permanence.

Here the context summarises some links of the long struggle between Moses and Pharaoh. Now there is an allusion to the flight and deliverance of the Children of Israel and the drowning of Pharaoh, and comments are then made on it. In the life of the barzakh, his condition will be as follows.

﴿The Fire; they are exposed to it morning and evening. And on the day the Hour comes [it will be said]: "Admit the people of Pharaoh into the most severe punishment."﴾ (40:46) This verse points to the fact that they are presented to the Fire morning and evening. In the period after their death and before the Resurrection, this will be the punishment of the grave, because after this there comes the phrase:

So the meaning is that in practice they are burned in the Fire morning and evening, and on the Day of Resurrection they will enter the most severe punishment permanently.

But in the next verse, the scene now is one in which the Resurrection is actually taking place. A glimpse of Hell is shown, where they dispute with one another:

It will not benefit them that they were mere followers and subordinates of others. It will not benefit them that they were being driven in the world like herds of sheep and goats, having no opinion, no will, and no authority.

Allah had given them a very great station, bestowed upon them human dignity and nobility, and this nobility was that every individual is responsible for his own deeds, and Allah gave every person freedom and liberty. But they themselves abandoned all these things and on their own began to follow those great and rebellious ones. Therefore, why do these people now complain against those leaders? Or rather, why do they even think about this complaint? Or rather, they have not thought about the complaint they are making. They say:

﴿"Indeed, we were your followers."﴾ (40:47) But they did not become followers, nor did they give up their freedom, for the sake of the hope that these leaders would intercede for them with Allah. Now those leaders are themselves burning in the Fire, and it is these leaders who brought them to this point, just as they used to drive them in the world, like herds of sheep and goats are driven. Among the servants, no one can reduce the punishment for any decree of Allah.

When both have come to know that no one except Allah can hear their plea, these people now go to the keeper of Hell, in the state of utter humiliation and extreme helplessness and destitution, and this condition has overtaken both the arrogant and the weak.

﴿And those in the Fire will say to the keepers of Hell: "Call upon your Lord to lighten for us a day of the punishment."﴾ (40:49) Now they will try to bring intercession from the keepers of Hell, so that they may present their request, placing their hopes in these attendants, because the punishment is severe, and [they say]: "You people get from the Lord merely a single day of forgiveness." In the period after their death and before the Resurrection, this will be the punishment of the grave, because after this there comes the phrase:

﴿And on the day the Hour comes [it will be said]: "Admit the people of Pharaoh into the most severe punishment."﴾ (40:46) Therefore, the punishment of being presented to the Fire is the punishment before the Resurrection, and it is a very severe penalty that they are presented to the Fire morning and evening. But they themselves abandoned all these things and on their own began to follow those great and rebellious ones. Therefore, why do these people now complain against those leaders? Or rather, why do they even think about this complaint? Or rather, they have not thought about the complaint they are making. They say:

﴿"Indeed, we were your followers."﴾ (40:47) But they did not become followers, nor did they give up their freedom, for the sake of the hope that these leaders would intercede for them with Allah. Now those leaders are themselves burning in the Fire, and it is these leaders who brought them to this point, just as they used to drive them in the world, like herds of sheep and goats are driven. Yet even so, they ask those leaders.

They know that these people have squandered their time. Therefore they rebuke them and inflict further pain, and tell them: now consider how you came to this wretched state.
