Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 40, verses 51–55:

Verses 51 to 55

This decisive commentary on this categorical position is very fitting. Mankind has come to know what the final outcome of the struggle between truth and falsehood always is: what the end of both is in this world, and what the end of both will be in the Hereafter. People have seen how Pharaoh and his chiefs ended in this world, just as they saw in the scene of the Resurrection that they were still quarrelling with one another in the Fire, and were left aside with utter contempt, as if of no concern. The decision of every struggle is this, just as the Qur'an clearly decides.

﴿Indeed, We shall surely help Our messengers and those who believe, in the life of this world and on the Day when the witnesses will stand up, the Day when the wrongdoers' excuses will not benefit them, and for them is the curse, and for them is the evil abode﴾ (40:51–52). Regarding the Hereafter, there is no room for debate on the part of any believer, and there is no matter on which argument may be made. As for help in this world, it needs explanation. In any case, Allah's decision and promise are certain; it is stated in definite words:

﴿Indeed, We shall surely help Our messengers and those who believe in the life of this world﴾ (40:51). Yet what people observe is that some of the messengers were killed, and some were expelled from their land. They had to leave their homes and their people and were driven out of their region. Among the believers, some are subjected to severe torment; some are burned in pits; some are martyred; some endure great grief and calamities. Then how is this definite promise, that We help Our messengers and the believers in the life of this world, to be understood? Through this question, Satan attacks the servants of Allah, and does what he does to them. So what is the reality?

The reality is that people know only the outward aspects of all matters. Most of the values and realities connected with Allah's system and decree are not before them. Moreover, people's thinking about deeds and their results is confined to a limited span of time, and the range of human conjecture and thought is limited. As for Allah's decisions, their scope in terms of time and place is vast. Allah does not discriminate between one age and another, nor does He distinguish between one region and another. If we move beyond the limits of time and place and reflect on the matter of faith, the reality that emerges is that faith prevails. The success of faith and belief is in truth the success of those who adopt faith and belief. There is no existence outside the people of faith. The first demand of faith is that those who bring it be annihilated in it: they must efface themselves and make faith prominent.

Furthermore, the concept of help is also limited among people. They look for the immediate help that they can see with their own eyes. But the forms of help are countless. Sometimes it appears to a person that help is defeat. Abraham (peace be upon him) was thrown into the fire, yet he did not turn away from his creed and his call. The question is: was he helped, or did he suffer defeat? Judged by the measures of faith, he was victorious. He was victorious when he was being thrown into the fire, and he was victorious when he was delivered. This is also a form of victory, and the fire becoming a garden is also one of its forms. Although the outward forms of the two are different, in their reality both are one. Husayn (may Allah be pleased with him) attained martyrdom at Karbala. It is a heart-rending event. Was this victory or defeat? If judged by limited outward measures, it was defeat. And if judged by the measures of truth, it is a great victory.

The killing of Husayn is in reality the death of Yazid.

Islam is revived after every Karbala.

Husayn is remembered with love to this day. To this day, people's hearts are with Husayn; to this day people sacrifice themselves for him, while the victor Yazid's name and trace have vanished. Shi'a and Sunni alike are devoted to Husayn, and no one says of Yazid that he is the son of Yazid or that he is Yazid himself.

There are many martyrs who, even had they lived for a thousand years, could not have spread their ideas. Yet through a single martyrdom their ideas spread to the ends of the world. No martyr can give the masses lofty aims through his speech and lectures, nor can he rouse the masses to lofty aims. But through his blood he delivers a sermon, and that is his final address. It becomes a perpetual motivator and remains a sign of the destination for generations. Sometimes the path that a single martyr marks out is followed by history for centuries, and caravans keep moving along that very road.

So what is victory, and what is defeat? We ought to re-examine the standards of victory and defeat that we have established in our minds, and then ask again where that help of Allah is, which Allah has promised to the believers, in this world and in the Hereafter. Yes, sometimes it happens that when the outward situation becomes compatible with Allah's lofty and far-reaching standards, immediate victory is also granted. Allah granted the Messenger Muhammad (peace be upon him) help and success during his own lifetime, because in the world the reality of the Islamic way of life and this help were established side by side. Help comes to a creed when the creed prevails over human society, and that society is dyed in its colour and is immersed in it. When an individual, a community and a ruling power are all immersed in it, then Allah helps such people and such a call, and this system and this way of life are re-established in their true form, and this system, having prevailed, leaves its imprint upon history. And these imprints of it are clearly visible in history. Thus the form of immediate help and the form of far-reaching purposes become joined together. Now immediate help appears apparently, and it is a part of the far-reaching sunnah of Allah. In this way a form of immediate victory arises within the sunnah of Allah and the decree of Allah.

There is another aspect of this matter that must be kept in view. Allah's promise stands with His messengers and those who believe. Therefore it is necessary that the reality of faith be firmly established and settled in the hearts of the believers who deserve the promise, so that Allah's promise may be fulfilled upon them. Regarding the reality of faith, people sometimes act with negligence. The reality of faith is that not even a trace of shirk remain in the heart of the believer; no kind of shirk should come near the heart. Some forms of shirk are extremely hidden. The heart becomes pure and clean from them only when a person turns exclusively to Allah alone, and relies upon Allah alone, and is content with whatever Allah decides about him. And a person surrenders himself to the decree of Allah. A person should feel that in his affairs only Allah is the disposer. Therefore, he should not be astonished in any state at what Allah chooses for him, and whatever befalls him he should accept with complete tranquillity, confidence, and submission. When a person reaches this station of submission and contentment, he does not go ahead of Allah, nor does he act hastily, and he does not present victory and help before Allah in the form he prefers. He hands over his affairs to Allah and remains firm on his path, and on that path he regards whatever comes before him as good. This is true help... This is victory over one's own self and one's own desires. This is inner victory, and the complete victory comes only when the inner victory is complete.

﴿Indeed, We shall surely help Our messengers and those who believe, in the life of this world and on the Day when the witnesses will stand up, the Day when the wrongdoers' excuses will not benefit them, and for them is the curse, and for them is the evil abode﴾ (40:51–52).

In the preceding scene we saw that no excuse is of any benefit to the wrongdoers. Their end was that they were cursed and became fuel for Hell. As for how Allah helps His messengers, one form of it is that Allah helped Moses (peace be upon him).

﴿And We certainly gave Moses the guidance, and We made the Children of Israel inherit the Book, a guidance and a reminder for people of understanding﴾ (40:53–54). This was an example of Allah's help: He gave Moses the Book, gave him guidance, and then gave him deliverance. Here the story of Moses is referred to only as an example. That story is very long, and it contains many instances of divine help and support.

After this example comes a final consolation, because the Muslims and the Messenger of Allah were living in very difficult circumstances in Makkah. They are being consoled that help will certainly come, and that the same consolation is also for those who, after the Messenger of Allah, are carrying out the work of the Islamic call and are in similar circumstances.

﴿So be patient; indeed the promise of Allah is true. And ask forgiveness for your sin, and glorify the praise of your Lord in the evening and the morning﴾ (40:55). O Prophet, be patient; Allah's promise is true. This is the final blow upon the strings of reason and wisdom. It is a call to patience: be patient with the denial of the people; be patient with the fact that falsehood holds power and is spreading because of it, though this is only for a period; be patient with the failings of people in their temperament, their conduct and their dealings; be patient with the self of man, its desires and its wishes. Especially when the self wishes that Allah's help should come very quickly, and the successes that result from help, and the difficulties created in the long struggle of the Islamic movement by friends even before enemies, be patient with them.

﴿So be patient; indeed the promise of Allah is true﴾ (40:55). "Better late than never." If your affairs are complicated, if outwardly the means of help do not appear, remember that it is the Divine Being who is making the promise of help, and who is able to clothe His promise in reality. And when Allah has promised, Allah has resolved.

﴿And ask forgiveness for your sin, and glorify the praise of your Lord in the evening and the morning﴾ (40:55). This is the true provision for the journey. The path is very long and arduous. Only one who keeps asking forgiveness for his faults can advance on it. Only one who keeps praising the Lord, and with praise glorifies and declares the purity of Allah, can go forward. In it one may receive help, and also the training of the human self; and also preparation for walking that path, and purification of the heart and sight. This is the help that works within the heart first, and after that the form of help appears that is manifest in practical life.

The mention of morning and evening is either because it denotes the whole time, since morning and evening are the two extremes of the day; or because at these times the human heart is clear and attentive, and the effects of reflection and of praising and glorifying Allah are deeper at these times.

This is the method through which Allah's help may be obtained, and Allah has appointed it as the means of granting His help. In accordance with it, preparation for walking this path will be made, the provision for the journey will be readied, and then help will come. For every battle, preparation and equipment are needed; no war can be fought without training and provisions.

When an individual, a community and a ruling power are all immersed in it, then Allah helps such people and such a call, and this system and this way of life are re-established in their true form, and this system, having prevailed, leaves its imprint upon history. Therefore, he should not be astonished in any state at what Allah chooses for him, and whatever befalls him he should accept with complete tranquillity, confidence, and submission. He hands over his affairs to Allah and remains firm on his path, and on that path he regards whatever comes before him as good. This is true help... That story is very long, and it contains many instances of divine help and support.

They are being consoled that help will certainly come, and that the same consolation is also for those who, after the Messenger of Allah, are carrying out the work of the Islamic call and are in similar circumstances.

O Prophet, be patient; Allah's promise is true. This is the final blow upon the strings of reason and wisdom. It is a call to patience: be patient with the denial of the people; be patient with the fact that falsehood holds power and is spreading because of it, though this is only for a period; be patient with the failings of people in their temperament, their conduct and their dealings; be patient with the self of man, its desires and its wishes. Especially when the self wishes that Allah's help should come very quickly, and the successes that result from help, and the difficulties created in the long struggle of the Islamic movement by friends even before enemies, be patient with them.

﴿So be patient; indeed the promise of Allah is true﴾ (40:55). "Better late than never." And when Allah has promised, Allah has resolved.

﴿And ask forgiveness for your sin, and glorify the praise of your Lord in the evening and the morning﴾ (40:55). This is the true provision for the journey. The path is very long and arduous. This is the help that works within the heart first, and after that the form of help appears that is manifest in practical life.

In accordance with it, preparation for walking this path will be made, the provision for the journey will be readied, and then help will come. For every battle, preparation and equipment are needed; no war can be fought without training and provisions.

Study Lesson 225: At a Glance

This lesson is fully connected in theme and subject with the previous one. It carries forward the subject left at the end of the previous lesson. The Messenger ﷺ is instructed to be patient with the way people unjustly reject the Islamic call. Patience, he is told, must be maintained. They harm him and prevent others from coming to Islam, and they do all this out of their false pride and arrogance. It is then explained that people dispute the signs of Allah without any proof or evidence. The real reason is that they are very small and insignificant, yet they regard themselves as very great, and this arrogance sits in their hearts and prevents them from accepting the truth.

Accordingly, they are made to consider: are you great, or is the universe that Allah created great? Reflect on the vastness of the heavens and on this earth, and you will see how small you are. The lesson proceeds to describe some of the signs of this universe and shows that these great signs have been subjected to this small and weak human being. It is further explained that consider the bounties and favours Allah has bestowed upon the human self. Are these not complete evidence of the existence of Allah alone, of His sovereignty and of His oneness? The Messenger ﷺ is told to proclaim the word of tawhid and turn away from the deities these people worship. The lesson concludes with a frightening scene from the scenes of the Day of Resurrection. To humiliate them, they will be asked there: where are those gods of yours? As with the end of the previous lesson, it concludes with the instruction to the Prophet ﷺ to be patient, whether Allah shows you some of the Islamic revolution's outcome or takes you away, before victory comes. The matter is in the hands of Allah, and all will return to Allah.

Lesson 225: Explanation of the Verses

Verses 56 to 60

Man sometimes forgets himself; he forgets that he is a small and weak creature in this universe. He is not himself a source of strength, but derives his strength from the true source of strength, which is Allah. When his connection with Allah is severed, he begins to swell and puff up, to become haughty and rebellious. And it begins to settle in his heart that he is something very great, and this thinking is derived from Satan, who was expelled from the Divine Court because of this very pride; then Allah let him loose upon man, and he attacks him from every side.

This man then keeps disputing about the signs of Allah and engages in obstinacy. This obstinacy is a quality by which the nature of man is fully revealed. This type of man convinces himself and others that he is investigating the truth and debating because he is not satisfied, and that he does not have complete certainty. But Allah knows His servants well. He is All-Hearing and All-Seeing and knows the secrets of hearts. Allah decides that this is due to pride, merely because of considering oneself great. This pride settles in the heart and it prompts a person to dispute over a matter that is not open to dispute. It is this pride that impels a person to undertake works that are higher than the reality of man; man strives to reach a station that is above him and beyond human reality. Lesson 225: Explanation of the Verses

Verses 56 to 60

Man sometimes forgets himself; he forgets that he is a small and weak creature in this universe. He is not himself a source of strength, but derives his strength from the true source of strength, which is Allah. When his connection with Allah is severed, he begins to swell and puff up, to become haughty and rebellious. And it begins to settle in his heart that he is something very great, and this thinking is derived from Satan, who was expelled from the Divine Court because of this very pride; then Allah let him loose upon man, and he attacks him from every side.

This man then keeps disputing about the signs of Allah and engages in obstinacy. This obstinacy is a quality by which the nature of man is fully revealed. This type of man convinces himself and others that he is investigating the truth and debating because he is not satisfied, and that he does not have complete certainty. But Allah knows His servants well. He is All-Hearing and All-Seeing and knows the secrets of hearts. Allah decides that this is due to pride, merely because of considering oneself great. This pride settles in the heart and it prompts a person to dispute over a matter that is not open to dispute. It is this pride that impels a person to undertake works that are higher than the reality of man; man strives to reach a station that is above him and beyond human reality. Man has neither proof nor justification for it. Solely because of this pride he begins such high flights; such are these people.

*Inna alladhina ... humu bibalighihi* (40:56): "Indeed, those who dispute the signs of Allah without any authority that has come to them, there is nothing in their hearts but pride, which they will never attain." Had man understood this universe well, recognised his own self, and realised his station in this universe, he would have become content and would not have exceeded his position and rank. If he understood that he is one of these countless existences, and that just as this entire universe is bound by the command of the Lord, so is he too, and he too moves according to the system of Allah's decree and destiny which only Allah knows, and that his role in the universe is a fixed role, then, if he realised these truths, he would be content and at rest, his head would bow somewhat, humility would develop within him, and he would live in complete peace and security with himself, with this universe and with his environment.

*Fa-stadhi bi-llahi innahu huwa as-Sami' al-Basir* (40:56): "So seek refuge in Allah; indeed He is the All-Hearing, the All-Seeing." The advice to seek refuge in Allah against pride shows that it is a very vile and despicable trait, because refuge in Allah is sought from what is extremely vile and undesirable, which results in evil, corruption and affliction. And all of these things exist in pride. Pride is a calamity for the proud person himself and also a calamity for his environment. In a heart where there is pride, it is a torment for that heart, and it is a habit that hurts the hearts of others too. Therefore pride is a kind of evil and corruption from which it is necessary to seek refuge in Allah.

*Innahu huwa as-Sami' al-Basir* (40:56): "He is the All-Hearing, the All-Seeing." Pride prompts a person to actions that can be seen and makes him say things that can be heard. To be protected from it, place yourself under the guardianship of the One who hears and sees.

After this, man is told what his true station is in this great universe, and how small and weak he is compared with some of Allah's creations that man can see. Upon seeing these things that are mentioned here, man immediately acknowledges their immensity, and when their full reality becomes clear to him, his awareness becomes even firmer.

*La-khalqu as-samawati ... la-ya'lamuna* (40:57): "Certainly, the creation of the heavens and the earth is greater than the creation of mankind, but most people do not know." The heavens and the earth lie spread out before man, and he sees them. It is within man's power to determine his own worth in relation to them. When man learns his relation to this earth and heaven, the distances of the heavens and the magnitude of the celestial spheres, his head may bow, and it is also possible that, through awareness of his own insignificance, he melts away, unless he remembers the honour that Allah has placed within him, on account of which man has been made honoured. That is the only quality by which man can stand before the greatness of this universe, for the universe is very great and awesome and he is very small.

A single moment of reflection upon this great universe is enough for man to know all this. This earth on which we live is a small star among the stars that follow the sun. The number of stars that follow this sun is in the millions, and this earth is one million times smaller than the sun. Then this sun is one of a hundred million such suns in the nearest galaxy to us, and we too are in this same galaxy. Mankind has so far discovered a hundred million galaxies floating in this vast space, and it may be that these are only a very small part of that space.

As far as human knowledge is concerned, man has discovered only a brief and noteworthy part of the universe, and even this small part is so vast that merely imagining it makes a person's head spin. We are about 93 million miles away from our sun, and this sun is the leader of the family of this small earth of ours. This earth too is 93 million miles away from its mother's lap, that is, the sun. This earth has separated from the sun itself.

The galaxy in whose domain this sun lies has a diameter of about one hundred thousand million light-years. A light-year is six hundred million miles, because the speed of light is 186,000 miles per second.

And the galaxy nearest to ours is one million seven hundred and fifty thousand light-years away. We must keep in view here that these distances and magnitudes are those which this insignificant human being has discovered, and along with this man has also discovered that it is only a very small part of reality. Therefore Allah, the Exalted, says:

*La-khalqu as-samawati ... la-ya'lamuna* (40:57): "Certainly, the creation of the heavens and the earth is greater than the creation of mankind, but most people do not know." The power of Allah makes no matter great or small, difficult or easy. He creates everything with a single word. These qualities belong to things. People see them as small or great, easy or difficult. Then what is the relation between man and this universe which causes such bewilderment? Despite such insignificance, man still has this pride!

*Wa-ma yastawi al-a'ma wa al-basir ...* (40:58): "The blind and the seeing are not equal, nor are those who believe and do righteous deeds equal to the evildoer." The one who has sight sees and has knowledge, and knows his own worth. He does not exceed his limits, does not swell up, and does not behave arrogantly. He sees and understands. The blind man neither sees nor knows his own worth; he knows neither his own position nor his relation to his environment. So, first of all, he judges himself wrongly; then he makes a wrong decision about his environment; and because of these misjudgements, he goes astray. In this way, the believer and the righteous person and the evildoer cannot be equal. The believers are those who see and know; therefore they make a correct assessment of themselves and their environment, whereas the disbeliever and the evildoer are ignorant. They ruin everything: themselves, their environment, other people, and above all they ruin their own deeds and understanding. They cannot harmonise with their environment. They are blind, blind in their hearts.

*Qalilan ma tatadhakkarun* (40:58): "Yet you remember very little." If we understood, we would know the truth. The matter is clear; only a reminder is needed. If we held firm certainty in the Hereafter, remembered it, kept the stations of the Resurrection in mind, and kept our presence there in our minds, we would be firm believers.

*Inna as-sa'ata ... la-yu'minun* (40:59): "Indeed, the Hour is coming; there is no doubt in it, but most people do not believe." This is why they dispute the signs of Allah and act with arrogance. Otherwise, if they believed and were certain, they would recognise the truth. They would know what their standing is with respect to the truth. Therefore they would not transgress.

Turning solely towards Allah, worshipping Him, and calling upon Him with utmost humility protects a person from that pride which causes him to swell up and to dispute the signs of Allah without any authority. Allah opens His doors for us so that we may turn to Him and call upon Him, and He declares that He has written upon Himself the acceptance of the prayer of everyone who calls upon Him. And He warns those who act arrogantly in the face of His call that they will be humiliated in the Fire.

*Wa-qala rabbukumu ... dakhirin* (40:60): "Your Lord says: Call upon Me, and I will respond to you. Indeed, those who are too arrogant to worship Me will enter Hell humiliated." It should be remembered that prayer also has its etiquette, and it is necessary to keep it in view. The heart must be sincere for Allah; one should ask without fixing a particular form; and one should ask with the certainty that Allah surely accepts. One should not fix the circumstances, times or places of acceptance, for that is entirely contrary to the etiquette of prayer. And one should believe that the ability to pray is granted by Allah alone. This too is a blessing; acceptance is another blessing. Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) said: "I do not carry the burden of wondering whether my prayer will be answered; my responsibility is to call upon Allah. When I am granted the ability and it is inspired in me that I should pray, then acceptance is already with it." Prayer is the matter of the heart of the knower of Allah; the knower knows that the God who decreed the prayer also decides its acceptance. When Allah grants the ability, prayer and acceptance are in harmony, in accord, and go together.

As for those who act arrogantly against turning towards Allah, their punishment is that they will be cast into Hell, humiliated and disgraced. And this is the punishment for pride that Allah has ordained, the pride by which man swells up: a small human being on this small earth and in this small life. This person forgets the great creation of Allah, forgets the greatness of Allah, and forgets the Hereafter, though it is coming, and there he will have to fall into Hell, humiliated and disgraced.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 40, verses 61–64 (part 1 of 2):

Verses 61 to 64

The passing of night and day are two cosmic phenomena, while the earth and the heavens are two cosmic creations. Mentioning these two here, it is then stated that in this night and day and in the earth and heavens, Allah created your beautiful forms and then created for you various kinds of sustenance in this world. This is your Lord, and these are His works. Blessed is the Lord of the worlds! He is the Living, and there is no living one besides Him, and all of this is His grace. Therefore, regarding Allah as One without partner, worship only Him. From this it becomes evident that these cosmic phenomena, these creational signs, and these creations of Allah must be read in a broad context in relation to the Oneness of Allah and His system of life, must be reflected upon, and their connection with Tawhid and the Shari'ah must be found. And one must observe what the harmony is within this creational system.

The way Allah has built this universe, and then the natural law (nāmūs-i-fitrat) according to which He has run it, is the same Allah who ran life on this spherical earth and arranged its development and growth. Then it is the same Divine Being who gave man his present form which we see. And He kept in this universe the matters necessary for the creation and life of man. It is He who made the night for tranquillity, rest and comfort. And He made the day bright, helpful for seeing, and for running about. And He made the earth fit for life and fit for walking about, and made the sky like a roof, that it holds on high the planets and stars, which do not fall. And their distances too would collide with one another and cause disturbance. If those distances were to change again, then disorder would arise in the existence of man on this small spherical earth. It is Allah who created pure food on this earth. He produced this sustenance from this very earth. This sustenance descends from the heavens in the form of rains, and people benefit from it. And how beautiful and varied are human forms! Then it is He who created in man those capacities which are in harmony with this universe. And these capacities are sufficient for living on this earth. Then these capacities are also in harmony with this entire universe. So all these matters are interconnected and in accord, as every person can observe. This is why the Qur'an takes all these matters in one place, in this very order and connection, and presents them as a decisive proof of His Oneness. And in the light of these matters it invites the human heart to call upon Allah alone, and to establish the religion and system of life for Him alone. And at the end it is said: All praise is due to Allah, Lord of the worlds! And it is decided that the Lord of the worlds can only be that Being who created all these things in this manner. This is the Ilah, the Lord of the worlds. So it is astonishing how people turn away from this great truth.

Here we give, in brief, glimpses which will themselves show that these matters have been taken into account in the structure of this universe and in its relationship with human life. A few moments in the direction of the truth which Allah has pointed to here:

"This earth is rotating on its axis in front of the sun, as a result of which the system of night and day has come into being. If its speed of rotation were slightly faster than its present speed, all houses would collapse, the parts of this earth would separate from one another and scatter into the atmosphere of the sky."

"And if this earth were to reduce the present speed of its axial rotation even a little, people would die from heat or cold. The present axial rotation of the earth has been made such that it is in harmony with animal and plant life on this earth, and beneficial to them in its broad meanings."

"And if the earth's axial rotation were to stop altogether, the vapours would disappear and the seas would become empty of waters."

"If the earth were to end its axial rotation and continue its annual rotation around the sun, what would happen? All crops would be destroyed, people would not know where the summers are and when the winters came, and spring and autumn would end."

"If the earth's crust were a few steps thicker, then due to the absorption of some gases, vegetation would be destroyed."

"The atmospheric layer above the earth, at its present height, if it were to become higher still, then the meteors which burn in the air today in millions, all of them would begin to fall upon the earth. Their speed is 46 miles per second. In this way they would burn everything on the earth that is capable of burning. And even if these meteors moved at the speed of a rifle bullet, all of them would still strike the earth, and the results would be extremely frightful. As for the poor human being, if even a small meteor whose speed is seventy times that of a rifle bullet were to strike this earth, the heat produced by the passage of that meteor alone would scatter the components of its body."

"At present the proportion of oxygen in the air is 21 percent. If it were to become 50 percent, all things capable of burning would catch fire and be consumed. With the mere spark of a flame, all the forests would burn, rather they would blow up in an instant. If the oxygen of the air were to decrease to 10 percent or less, the life of the earth might perhaps adapt itself to it after a long period, but all the conveniences by which man is considered civilised would disappear, such as fire, and so on."

In short, in the creation and formation of this universe, thousands of such supportive and helpful things are seen placed with systematic planning, such that if any one of them were to suffer even a slight disturbance, our life would not remain in its present form. Likewise, the present form of the life of other animals would also not remain.

As for man, his beautiful and lovely form is of such a kind that it is unique in its manner and distinguished among all living things. It is such a perfect and complete creation that it performs all its duties with great ease and precision. This creation of his, his movement upon the earth, and the conditions in which it has been made easy for him to live and work, then his supreme and exalted distinction by which he has been made the chief of all creatures of the earth and given the office of khilafah on the earth, and for the fulfilment of the duties of that office he has been endowed with intellect and understanding, and then he has been honoured with a connection with the Lord Most High. These are indeed the most distinguished qualities of man.

Now let us turn to the self of man, and consider the subtlety of his organs and their functions, which is also the meaning of this verse:

﴿وَصَوَّرَكُمْ فَأَحْسَنَ صُوَرَكُمْ﴾ (40:64) "He shaped you and shaped you well." So we must study each of the small organs of man, indeed we must discuss each cell of man's cells.

From a single example one can perceive the deep technology of human creation and the human body. Take the human jaw, and the placement of teeth within it. If viewed from the angle of an instrument of food, they are so sensitive that if the tongue or saliva is raised even within a limit of 1/10 millimetre, the jaws resist the tongue and saliva. And if any tooth is raised to the same extent, it begins to collide with the body opposite it. And if a paper as thick as a cigarette paper comes between the two jaws, it will feel the pressure of both jaws. And even then there will be pressure from both jaws, because the structure of the two jaws is such that when they meet, the teeth on both sides fit fully into one another. Thus they perform the act of drinking and chewing, and they chew even things whose thickness is as thin as the rough paper of a cigarette.

Then, for this same human being, with this structure of his, provisions have been made to live on this earth, so that he may remain alive here. Therefore, regarding Allah as One without partner, worship only Him. And one must observe what the harmony is within this creational system.

The way Allah has built this universe, and then the natural law (nāmūs-i-fitrat) according to which He has run it, is the same Allah who ran life on this spherical earth and arranged its development and growth. Then it is the same Divine Being who gave man his present form which we see. And He kept in this universe the matters necessary for the creation and life of man. Therefore, regarding Allah as One without partner, worship only Him. And one must observe what the harmony is within this creational system.

The way Allah has built this universe, and then the natural law (nāmūs-i-fitrat) according to which He has run it, is the same Allah who ran life on this spherical earth and arranged its development and growth. Then it is the same Divine Being who gave man his present form which we see. And He kept in this universe the matters necessary for the creation and life of man. It is He who made the night for tranquillity, rest and comfort. And He made the day bright, helpful for seeing, and for running about. And He made the earth fit for life and fit for walking about, and made the sky like a roof, that it holds on high the planets and stars, which do not fall. And their distances too would collide with one another and cause disturbance. If those distances were to change again, then disorder would arise in the existence of man on this small spherical earth. "If the earth's crust were a few steps thicker, then due to the absorption of some gases, vegetation would be destroyed."

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 40, verses 67–68:

Verses 67 to 68

Human beings cannot comprehend the creation of man on this earth through human knowledge, because man did not exist at the time he was created. Among the successive stages of human creation there are some matters which man observes, but this human observation has come to light in its present developed form only in the present age, centuries after the revelation of the Qur'an.

The first matter is that man was created from clay, and this event took place at a time when man did not exist. But it has become known that clay is the foundation of life on this earth. Man was made from it and was given life from it. No one except Allah knows how this miracle came into being, and at what time and in what manner this great event in the history of life and the earth occurred. As for the continuation of generations, its system has been arranged so that the male cell, that is the sperm (nutfah), when it meets the female's ovum, and the two unite and settle in the womb in the form of a clot of blood, the embryo (janin) passes through its stages, and in its final stage the child emerges. Before birth, very great transformations continue to take place in the child. If the initial cell is observed closely, its life is longer than the life of the child, that is, from birth to death. In the context of the discourse, the Qur'an has mentioned here only some of its distinctive qualities and stages, namely the stage of childhood, then reaching the age of maturity, that is, the age of thirty, then old age. These are the stages through which man passes, moving from his weakness, between the beginning and the end, to his full strength.

"Wa minkum man yutawaffa min qabl" (40:67): "Among you is one who is taken back before." That is, he does not pass through all these stages, or some stages are skipped for him, and he dies.

"Wa li-tablughu ajalan musamma" (40:67): "All this is done so that you may reach your appointed term." This term is fixed, determined and known. There is no advancing or delay in it.

"Wa la'allakum ta'qilun" (40:67): "And so that you may understand the truth." The passage of the embryo, then the passage of the child, then the beauty of their form and the correct estimates of their natural growth and development, is a great provision for thinking in its patterns.

The journey of the embryo is indeed a most astonishing journey. After the progress of medical sciences, we have acquired astonishing information about it. Embryology is an independent discipline. Yet the way in which the Qur'an, more than fourteen hundred years ago, pointed with such precise estimation to some of its stages is something that grips thought and insight. It is not possible for a human being to pass through these stages heedlessly and not reflect deeply upon them. The journey of the embryo and the journey of the child leave deep impressions on human sensibility and strongly shake the human heart, whatever stage of intellect and maturity a person may be in. Every generation of humankind is affected by it according to its knowledge, and therefore the Qur'an has drawn the attention of human generations to this, because man is affected by it. After this, he is free: whether he responds or does not respond.

After this discussion, here is an instructive comment on giving life, causing death, creation and development:

"Huwa-lladhi... kun fa-yakun" (40:68): "He is the One who gives life and causes death. When He decides any matter, He merely commands it, 'Be,' and it is." The Qur'an mentions the signs of life and death often, because the theme of life and death profoundly affects the human personality. These are most prominent and repeatedly recurring events, and human senses observe them very closely. At first glance, what a person understands from giving life and causing death is one thing, but on closer examination the meaning of life and death is far deeper than that. There are many kinds of life, and there are many kinds of death. We see the earth as dead, and then we see the same earth alive and verdant. When it is dead, the trees have no leaves, the branches appear dry; that is one thing, the season. And when they come to life, these same dead branches and twigs become green and flourishing and sway in bloom. The branches burst forth at every joint, and flowers and leaves emerge. It seems as though life gushes forth from those branches. Look at an egg, then look at a chick; look at a seed and at the plant that sprouts; and then look at the reverse journey, how this same life turns into death and fields lie flattened. All these conditions affect the heart and the mind, and according to the saying "Every person's thought is according to his capacity," each person is impressed in his own way. Finally, beyond life and death, comes the important question of how the universe came into being: simply, Allah willed, the command "Be" was given, and everything came to be, or whatever He wished came to be. The universe kept coming into being, and continuity kept being established. "Fa-tabaraka Allahu ahsan al-khaliqin" (blessed is Allah, the best of creators).

After this scene of life and death, and after the "Be" of origination and creation, disputation, argument and quarrelling over the signs and bounties of Allah are fruitless and very strange, and the rejection of the message and call of the messengers is stranger still. Now, be warned! A terrifying scene is about to come before you. Beware! This is the Resurrection, and you are going to see that scene; before you see it, see it now!

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 40, verses 67–68:

Verses 67 to 68

Human beings cannot comprehend the creation of man on this earth through human knowledge, because man did not exist at the time he was created. Among the successive stages of human creation there are some matters which man observes, but this human observation has come to light in its present developed form only in the present age, centuries after the revelation of the Qur'an.

The first matter is that man was created from clay, and this event took place at a time when man did not exist. But it has become known that clay is the foundation of life on this earth. Man was made from it and was given life from it. No one except Allah knows how this miracle came into being, and at what time and in what manner this great event in the history of life and the earth occurred. As for the continuation of generations, its system has been arranged so that the male cell, that is the sperm (nutfah), when it meets the female's ovum, and the two unite and settle in the womb in the form of a clot of blood, the embryo (janin) passes through its stages, and in its final stage the child emerges. Before birth, very great transformations continue to take place in the child. If the initial cell is observed closely, its life is longer than the life of the child, that is, from birth to death. In the context of the discourse, the Qur'an has mentioned here only some of its distinctive qualities and stages, namely the stage of childhood, then reaching the age of maturity, that is, the age of thirty, then old age. These are the stages through which man passes, moving from his weakness, between the beginning and the end, to his full strength.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 40, verses 69–76:

Verses 69–76

This refers to the earlier verses: despite the signs of Allah that have appeared, the attitude of those who still dispute about His signs is surprising, but the end that awaits them is extremely instructive!

﴿Have you not seen those who dispute concerning the signs of Allah? From where are they being turned away? Those who denied the Book and that with which We sent Our messengers.﴾ (40:69–70)

They had only denied the Qur'an and the Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ), but by doing so they denied all the Books and all the Messengers, because the creed of Tawhid (affirmation of Allah's oneness) was one for all the messengers, and this creed was given in its complete form to the Seal of the Prophets (ﷺ). Therefore they had in effect denied prophethood and all the messengers. Every denier has done the same, whether in ancient or modern times; each has denied the creed of Tawhid.

﴿But they will come to know.﴾ (40:70) That is, they will soon learn what their end will be. The following verses give details of the fate of such people: they will be punished in a manner that is extremely humiliating and degrading; there will not merely be punishment, but disgrace will be added to it.

﴿When the shackles and chains are around their necks, and they are dragged.﴾ (40:71) They will be dragged as cattle are dragged, in disgrace. Why should they be honoured? They themselves cast off the garment of honour. Thus, dragged in humiliation and cried out at, they will at last be thrown into scalding water and fire.

﴿In scalding water, then in the Fire they will be set ablaze.﴾ (40:72) That is, they will be bound, then, with chains on their necks as dogs are led, they will be driven and thrown into a place filled with scalding water and fire.

In this state they will receive rebuke, reproach and scorn:

﴿Then it will be said to them, "Where are those you used to associate with Allah?"﴾ (40:73) Then they will answer in the manner of one who has been deceived and then realises the deception, and who is deeply despairing and harmed:

﴿They will say, "They have strayed from us; rather, we did not used to invoke anything before."﴾ (40:74) They will say that those gods have vanished from them so completely that they no longer know any way to find them, and they no longer show them the way. Rather, what they used to call upon before were nothing at all; they were mere illusions and fables. Upon this despairing answer comes this comment and lesson:

﴿Thus does Allah lead astray the disbelievers.﴾ (40:74) After this comes further rebuke and the reason for their misguidance.

﴿That is because you used to exult in the earth without right and because you used to be insolent. Enter the gates of Hell, to abide therein forever. How wretched is the abode of the arrogant.﴾ (40:75–76) They will be told: "This is your end because you were absorbed in what is not right on earth, and then you exulted in it. Now go, enter the gates of Hell, where you shall remain forever; how evil is the dwelling-place of the arrogant." O Helper of the helpless, where are they being taken with these chains and shackles around their necks, into scalding water and fire? It appears that before the eternal torment of Hell, they will be made to suffer the torment of scalding water and fire.

﴿So how wretched is the abode of the arrogant!﴾ (40:76) The real cause of this humiliating punishment that is being inflicted upon them is arrogance, and because of that arrogance, contempt and abasement have been added to this severe punishment.

After this frightful scene of punishment and degrading treatment, which fell upon them as a consequence of their unjust disputing over the signs of Allah, and whose real cause was arrogance, which puffs a person up, after this scene and this evil end, the Messenger (ﷺ) is admonished to be patient, for the arrogance and disputing of these people cause him great distress. He is consoled that the promise of Allah is true, whether the promise of the Islamic revolution is fulfilled in his lifetime or later; it is Allah's pleasure to act as He wills, and the Messenger's task is to convey the message and then go to his Lord.

Now go, enter the gates of Hell, where you shall remain forever; how evil is the dwelling-place of the arrogant." O Helper of the helpless, where are they being taken with these chains and shackles around their necks, into scalding water and fire? It appears that before the eternal torment of Hell, they will be made to suffer the torment of scalding water and fire.

﴿So how wretched is the abode of the arrogant!﴾ (40:76) The real cause of this humiliating punishment that is being inflicted upon them is arrogance, and because of that arrogance, contempt and abasement have been added to this severe punishment.

After this frightful scene of punishment and degrading treatment, which fell upon them as a consequence of their unjust disputing over the signs of Allah, and whose real cause was arrogance, which puffs a person up, after this scene and this evil end, the Messenger (ﷺ) is admonished to be patient, for the arrogance and disputing of these people cause him great distress. He is consoled that the promise of Allah is true, whether the promise of the Islamic revolution is fulfilled in his lifetime or later; it is Allah's pleasure to act as He wills, and the Messenger's task is to convey the message and then go to his Lord.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 40, verse 77:

Verse No. 77

This is a glimpse, and we should pause and reflect on it. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was, in that period, enduring arrogance, harm, denial and disobedience from his opponents. He is instructed that his duties are these, and that he should confine himself to them. As for the outcomes, the responsibility lies with Allah, even if he desires to see the deniers and the arrogant punished in this world. Your duty is to carry out the command and to discharge your obligation, for bringing a matter to its conclusion is not the task of the caller (dā'iyah). It is in Allah's authority, and He does whatever He wills.

O Lord of the worlds! How lofty this station is, and how perfect the etiquette taught to those who are engaged in the work of calling to Islam. And who are they? The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and his companions!

This command is very heavy upon the human self. It is a command that goes against the desires of weak human beings. For this reason, patience is enjoined here even before this command is given. Therefore, the repeated instruction to be patient here is not a repetition; it is a patience of a new kind. This patience is harder than patience under harm, denial and mockery. To tell all callers, human and mortal callers, that your enemies will certainly be punished, that Allah will surely seize them, but perhaps you may not see it, is contrary to the human desire to see one's enemies punished. This is an intense desire, especially when the callers are being subjected to oppression. Yet these are the etiquettes of Allah, and this is the training by Allah of His servants who have been given choice, and it is desired to purify the human self from everything that contains even the slightest desire, even if this desire is merely that the enemies of the religion be punished.

All the callers of the religion should reflect on this point, whatever time and place they may be in: amid the storms of desires, this is the anchor of success. Those desires appear very pure at the beginning, but in the end Satan slips into them.

**Lesson No. 226: At a Glance**

This entire lesson completes and explains the lesson of admonition that comes at the end of the previous lesson. The Prophet (ﷺ) and the believers were instructed to be patient in the difficulties of the path, until the command of Allah arrives and the promise of Allah regarding the victory of Islam is fulfilled, whether during the lifetime of the Prophet (ﷺ) or after his death. This is because the authority is not in the hand of the Prophet (ﷺ). Rather, the matter concerns Islam, those who believe in it, and their opponents and disputants. Both sides are at war, and the decision between them rests with Allah. It is Allah who drives the movement of the Islamic revolution, in the manner He wills.

The lesson with which this surah concludes presents this reality in another form: that the struggle between disbelief and Islam is not a new matter, nor did it begin with the mission of Muhammad (ﷺ) and Islam. Messengers were sent before him (ﷺ); some of their stories have been related to you and some have not. All of them were received with denial and rejection. Each was asked to bring miracles, and each of them wished that Allah would manifest some miracle that those who denied would see and believe. But the manifestation of miracles is by the command of Allah, and it occurs when Allah wills. This call is the call of Allah, and He drives it in the manner He wills. However, some of the miracles of Allah lie scattered throughout this universe, visible to the people of every time and place, such as cattle, ships, and other things that no one can deny.

This lesson concludes with a very severe jolt, showing the destruction of those peoples who denied before, and who remained proud of their wealth, their riches and their progress. Then Allah seized them according to His sunnah:

﴿فَلَمَّا رَأَوْا بَأْسَنَا قَالُوا آمَنَّا بِاللَّهِ وَحْدَهُ وَكَفَرْنَا بِمَا كُنَّا بِهِ مُشْرِكِينَ * فَلَمْ يَكُ يَنفَعُهُمْ إِيمَانُهُمْ لَمَّا رَأَوْا بَأْسَنَا ۖ سُنَّتَ اللَّهِ الَّتِي قَدْ خَلَتْ فِي عِبَادِهِ ۖ وَخَسِرَ هُنَالِكَ الْكَافِرُونَ﴾ (40: 78)

"But when they saw Our punishment, their faith could not benefit them after they had seen Our punishment. This is the established way of Allah which has always been among His servants. And there the disbelievers lost."

**Lesson No. 226: Explanation of the Verses**

**Verse No. 78**

Examples of the struggle to establish the religion and examples of the sending of prophets exist in the previous history. Some of their accounts are related in the Qur'an and some are not mentioned, and for those whose accounts exist in previous history, some are mentioned in the Qur'an and some are not. Those accounts which are related contain the signposts of the long struggle of the Islamic movement. This path is clear, long, and reaches its destination. The accounts of these prophets clearly show what the sunnah of Allah is and what the duty of the messengers is. The point that needs to be emphasized is also clarified, which the caller should rely upon, namely:

﴿وَمَا كَانَ لِرَسُولٍ أَن يَأْتِيَ بِآيَةٍ إِلَّا بِإِذْنِ اللَّهِ﴾ (40: 78)

"It was not for any messenger to bring a sign except by permission of Allah."

It is a strong human desire, even if the one who has it is a messenger, that the opponents of the Islamic call should accept the call, and that the stubborn and arrogant people should believe in it. Therefore, human souls naturally desire the manifestation of miracles, so that the tongues of the opponents are silenced and they believe. But Allah's wish is that His chosen servants should rely on patience and keep you steadfast in the call. This is expressed by saying that the matter of victory and defeat is not in your hands. Your task is to convey the call. As for showing a miracle, that is Allah's task; when Allah wills, the miracle will come. Be assured, remain firm, work with dedication, and be patient with the results that come from your hands, and leave the outcome of the call to Allah.

Here it is also made clear that people should know the reality of divinity and also understand the office of prophethood, and know that prophets too are humans. Allah has chosen them for the office of prophethood. A duty is assigned to them; they have neither the power nor the permission to go beyond the limits of their duties.

Furthermore, the delay in the arrival of miracles is a blessing for them, because the sunnah of Allah is that when miracles come and people deny them, Allah then destroys those peoples. Therefore, the non-arrival of a miracle is in reality a respite, and this respite is from Allah.

﴿فَإِذَا جَاءَ أَمْرُ اللَّهِ قُضِيَ بِالْحَقِّ وَخَسِرَ هُنَالِكَ الْمُبْطِلُونَ﴾ (40: 78)

"Then when the command of Allah comes, judgment will be given in truth, and there the falsifiers will lose."

Now no further opportunity for action or repentance or return remains, and the final decision is made.

Now those people who demand miracles are directed to those signs and miracles which lie scattered in this universe, and which, through seeing them day and night, humans have become so accustomed to that they are no longer miracles for them. It is said about them that if they were to reflect upon them, they would certainly not demand any further miracle. All these things are also signs of Allah's divinity, because there is no one other than Allah who can claim that he created them, and likewise this claim is rejected at first sight, that this whole universe came into existence by itself.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 40, verses 79–80:

Verses 79 to 81

The initial creation of these livestock is a sign in the same way that the creation of man is a sign and a miracle. Breathing life into these animals, fashioning them in this form and shape, and creating them in varied colours are all miracles. Then, all these beasts and livestock have been made subservient to man, although some of them are stronger than man both in body and in strength, but

﴿It is Allah who has made for you the cattle, that you may ride some of them and eat some of them﴾ (40:79). Now, if someone says that these animals came into existence in this way and that they are no miracle for man, or that animals do not point to a Creator who brought them into being and made them subservient to man, and that these animals possess these characteristics and that human beings also possess these characteristics, then such statements are not acceptable, and the natural thinking of man rejects them. Therefore, those who make such statements are very superficial people, and their statements are entirely superficial and mere disputation.

They are reminded of what supernatural miracles and what blessings are in these verses.

﴿That you may reach upon them a need that is in your hearts, and upon them and upon ships you are carried﴾ (40:80). ﴿That you may ride upon some of them and eat some of them. And for you in them are [other] benefits, and that you may reach upon them a need that is in your hearts. And upon them and upon ships you are carried﴾ (40:79–80). They were the desires that were in their hearts, and they reached them by riding these animals. These were very great needs and requirements, especially in that era, when there were no modern means of transport. Even today these animals fulfil some needs. Even today there are some mountains so rugged that no aeroplane, no train, no motor vehicle goes there. Only these animals reach there. The paths in those mountains are so narrow that only these animals can manage them.

﴿And upon them and upon ships you are carried﴾ (40:80). These two are among the signs of Allah and among the blessings that He bestowed upon man. He made the ship travel on water. These are the properties that were placed in water and in the ship at the time of creation, on earth and in the heavens, on land and at sea. Whether this ship moves by sails, by steam, by atomic power, or by some other power that Allah has placed in this universe and granted man the capacity to put those powers to use, all these things have been brought within the theme of Allah's miracles and the blessings He has bestowed. Many such signs and miracles lie scattered throughout this universe. It is not possible for a human being to deny any of these miracles and blessings, provided he is serious.

﴿He shows you His signs, so which of the signs of Allah will you deny?﴾ (40:81). Yes, there are some people who deny. Some are those who dispute concerning the signs of Allah, and some are those who bring false arguments so that through them they may bring the truth down. But none of them is righteous; either there is crookedness in him, or some self-interest, or arrogance, or he is under some delusion, or he is doing this for some other purpose.

Some people dispute because they are powerful, arrogant and oppressive like Pharaoh and others. They fear for their rule and authority, they fear for their throne and crown. The call to truth overturns the foundations upon which these thrones and crowns are established, because the Islamic call's principle is that there is one deity and one ruler.

Some people dispute because they are religious leaders. Some dispute because they want a particular system of government and economy, such as the standard-bearers of communism, when a heavenly creed and belief does not make a person a slave and does not free him from the servitude of Allah and enslave him to another ideology or another leader.

Some people dispute because they want to be free of priestcraft, as happened in medieval times between the Church and the common people. Since the common people wanted to be free of priestcraft, they also returned to the Church its deity, because in the name of deity the priests had kept people enslaved.

Apart from these causes there are many other causes, but the natural thinking of man rejects all these causes and accepts the reality which permanently exists in the existence of this universe, and whose presence is indicated by these signs of the universe. And at the end, this powerful remark:

The Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 40, verses 81–85:

Verses 81 to 85

In human history, the destruction of past nations is preserved through narrations; the stories of some are preserved in the pages of books. The Qur'an repeatedly draws attention to these Ayyam Allah (the Days of Allah). This is because the path on which humanity has advanced contains facts scattered everywhere. Moreover, the impact of these Ayyam Allah on a human being is very profound. And since the Qur'an is being revealed from the One who created human nature (fitrah), it speaks while keeping the demands of human nature in view. The Qur'an is thoroughly familiar with the way of human nature. Allah knows what this creation of His is affected by, and in what manner a matter can be conveyed into its heart. Allah knows which door of the human heart opens with a single knock, which door opens with several forceful knocks, and which door has rusted and does not open without being broken.

Allah asks human beings, and they are encouraged to take a tour of human history: come, look with open eyes at the rises and falls of human history. Wander through every valley, keep your sensitivity alive, and walk with your heart and sight opened. See and reflect: what has happened on this earth before you, and what calamities have befallen humanity.

*Afalam yasiru... min qablihim* (40:82): "Have they not travelled through the earth and seen what was the end of those before them?" Before the end of those nations is described, some of their features are mentioned and their conditions of life are compared, so that the lesson is complete.

*Kanu akthara... fil-ard* (40:82): "They were more numerous than these, greater in strength, and left behind more magnificent traces in the earth." In number, in political power and in development, they were superior to the people present. Among them were several generations that passed before the Arabs. Some of their stories were related to the Messenger, some were left buried in the graveyard of history, and some stories were known to the Arabs, while the traces of some they saw day and night.

*Fama aghna 'anhum ma kanu yaksibun* (40:82): "So what they had earned did not avail them at all." Neither their multitude, nor their strength, nor their development could save them, even though they relied upon these very things and were arrogant. Rather, these same things became the cause of their destruction.

*Falamma ja'at-hum rusuluhum bil-bayyinati farihu bima 'indahum minal-'ilm* (40:83): "When their messengers came to them with clear proofs, they rejoiced in the knowledge they had." Knowledge, when detached from faith, is a great trial. It blinds a person and makes him rebellious. Such apparent and scientific knowledge makes people arrogant, because such people think that by virtue of this knowledge they hold power, operate great forces, and are owners of great treasures. Thus they go beyond their limits and forget the vast expanses which their knowledge has not yet reached, although those expanses exist in this universe. They have not yet gained control over these forces, nor can they even conceive of them; they have only reached a mere edge of these vastnesses. Thus this faithless man of knowledge swells with pride and goes beyond his bounds. His knowledge puffs him up, and his ignorance makes him forget his true reality. If he had estimated that his knowledge is very little, that the domain of his ignorance is very vast, and that what he measures is very small compared with what he cannot even imagine, he would have bowed his head, cast off his greatness, and reduced somewhat this swelling of his. In any case, these people who became absorbed in their present knowledge kept mocking those who reminded them.

*Wa haqa bihim ma kanu bihi yastahzi'un* (40:83): "Then there descended upon them what they used to mock." When they saw the punishment of Allah, the veil was lifted, and they came to know that what they had been proud of was nothing. Now they acknowledged what they used to deny: they became believers in the oneness of Allah, and they disowned their associates; but by then the time had passed.

*Falamma ra'aw ba's-ana* (40:85): "When they saw Our punishment, they cried out: 'We believe in Allah alone, and we disbelieve in what we used to associate with Him.' But their faith was of no benefit to them after they had seen Our punishment." This is because it is the sunnah of Allah that faith is not accepted after the punishment has been seen, for at that time what appears is the repentance of fear, not the repentance of faith.

*Sunnatallahi allati qad khalat fi 'ibadihi* (40:85): "This is the established law of Allah which has always operated among His servants." The sunnah of Allah admits no change or alteration; it follows its fixed course.

*Wa khasira hunalika al-kafirun* (40:85): "At that time the disbelievers were lost."

This surah concludes with this severe scene, the scene of the punishment of Allah, in which they cry out, lament, beg for forgiveness, and proclaim faith and conviction. This conclusion of the surah is in harmony with its atmosphere, its themes and its subject matter.

During this surah we have discussed issues that are important themes of purely Meccan surahs, such as the question of tawhid, the question of resurrection (ma'ad), and the question of revelation (wahy). However, these issues were not the main subject of this surah. Its main subject was the battle between truth and falsehood, faith and disbelief, reform and rebellion. These were the prominent themes and subject matter of this surah, and these are its important features and, compared with all other surahs, its most prominent aims.
